Note: The recurring architectural split between a KnowledgeOS Kernel (protects invariants, never reasons) and Reasoning Engines (LLMs/TMS/solvers that explore and propose, validated at the kernel boundary); recurs in S0218, S0220, S0225 (as Semantic/Epistemic/Governance kernel triad).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Ātma is the persistent identity of a knowledge-bearing system across successive knowledge states, while its knowledge, understanding, observations, and forms may change over time.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Knowledge Ātma A_K as the persistent identity of a knowledge-bearing system across a sequence of knowledge states K_0,K_1,...,K_t, satisfying A_K(t1)=A_K(t2) while K_t1≠K_t2 in general — 'the Ātma remains invariant while the knowledge state evolves'. Explicitly NOT defined as 'all knowledge' or as the Ideal State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Knowledge Ātma}\neq K_t\neq I_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes three distinct concepts that must not collapse: Knowledge Ātma (who/what persists through knowledge-state changes), Knowledge State K_t (what is currently known/represented), Ideal State I_t (what should be known/understood/achieved for the current purpose) — Knowledge Ātma ≠ K_t ≠ I_t, called 'a very strong architectural separation'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t\subseteq\mathcal K
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a potentially unbounded Knowledge Space 𝒦 of which the current Knowledge State is only a finite/partial representation, K_t⊆𝒦; Knowledge Ātma is not 𝒦 itself but the persistent identity undertaking an 'epistemic journey' A_K --epistemic journey--> K_t⊆𝒦 across K_0->K_1->K_2->... indefinitely. Layered architecture diagram: Ātma=persistence/identity, Knowledge State=current manifestation, Zero=reveals the boundary of what is currently known, Lord=expands the possible knowledge horizon, Sārathi=navigates the transition, Knower=experiences/evaluates/decides.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Ātma is an architectural and mathematical abstraction inspired by the philosophical concept of Ātman. It is not a computational representation or proof of the metaphysical Ātman described in the Bhagavad Gītā.
a_rows_sample.statement: Issues an explicit disclaimer required before using the term in formal theory: Knowledge Ātma is an architectural/mathematical abstraction inspired by Ātman, not a computational representation or proof of the metaphysical Ātman — protecting the model from a category error. Notes that introducing Knowledge Ātma changes the ontology of the complete KnowledgeOS model, requiring formal distinction of identity, state, knowledge, understanding, ideal, and evolution, and recommends exploring this before Question 20.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ātma is the persistent Knower whose identity remains invariant while its knowledge, understanding, observations, experiences, and represented states change over time.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reconciles 'Ātma = invariant identity underlying changing states' with 'Ātma = the Knower' into one definition: Ātma = the persistent Knower, invariant (A_t1=A_t2) while its knowledge state K_t changes (K_t1≠K_t2). 'Knower' names its role, 'invariant/persistent' names its mathematical property.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \underbrace{\text{Ātma}}_{\text{Who knows}} \quad \underbrace{K_t}_{\text{What is known}} \quad \underbrace{I_t}_{\text{What should be known}}
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a clean three-way separation Ātma ('who knows') / K_t ('what is known') / I_t ('what should be known'), judged much cleaner than identifying Ātma with the Knowledge State itself; repeats the caution that this is a KnowledgeOS mathematical/architectural abstraction inspired by Ātman, not a claim of having mathematically captured the metaphysical Ātman of the Gītā.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ātma is not the entire KnowledgeOS kernel implementation. Rather, “Knowledge Ātma” can be the conceptual identity/principle of the kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge Ātma ≡(conceptual) the persistent identity/principle of the KnowledgeOS Kernel, while 'KnowledgeOS Kernel = the executable realization of that principle' — preserving the concept/implementation distinction. The kernel is what remains structurally stable while Knowledge State K_t, Epistemic State Σ_t and Investigation State Q_t evolve.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A_K = \operatorname{Invariant}(S_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives Ātma a formal manifestation: A_K = Invariant(S_t) where S_{t+1}=δ(S_t,o_t) — the system state evolves (S_0->S_1->S_2->...) while A_K remains invariant, giving architectural form to 'Ātma is the persistent Knower while the state changes'. Composes the full architecture: KnowledgeOS = Knowledge Ātma Kernel + Knowledge Space + Epistemic Capabilities + Domain Knowledge, with the Kernel managing/evolving K_t and K_t⊆𝒦.

a_rows_sample.anchor: we can distinguish two Ātma concepts
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes two Ātma concepts that must be given different names so they are never confused: Human/Knower Ātma 𝒜_H — the human Knower (e.g. Arjuna) who has intent, asks questions, observes, experiences uncertainty, evaluates meaning, decides, and acts, with changing knowledge state K^H_t but persistent subject; and KnowledgeOS Ātma 𝒜_K — the persistent identity/principle of the KnowledgeOS epistemic system/kernel that maintains and operates on its own knowledge states K^K_t via observation representation, evidence/provenance, dimension discovery, epistemic evaluation, Zero, coherence, state transition, investigation support.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would not yet say that KnowledgeOS Ātma is literally a second Ātman
a_rows_sample.statement: Cautions against treating KnowledgeOS Ātma as literally a second metaphysical Ātman — that would move from architectural analogy to metaphysical claim. Defines 𝒜_H := Human Knower abstraction and 𝒜_K := KnowledgeOS persistent system identity; the shared word 'Ātma' expresses the analogy of persistence/invariant identity, not metaphysical identity between the two.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal A_H \neq \mathcal A_K \neq K_t \subseteq \mathcal K
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes the four-way separation Knower Ātma ≠ Knowledge Ātma, Knowledge Ātma ≠ Knowledge State, Knowledge State ≠ Knowledge Space, giving 𝒜_H ≠ 𝒜_K ≠ K_t ⊆ 𝒦. Models the Arjuna-Sārathi interaction as 𝒜_H --Intent--> 𝒜_K --Investigation--> K_t --Zero--> Δ_t --Sārathi--> next inquiry, worked through 'show me whom I have to fight' discovering new dimensions {Kinship, Teacher, Elder,...} via parsing/semantic reconstruction rather than the Knower pre-specifying them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What is the exact relationship between the Human Knower Ātma and the KnowledgeOS Ātma?
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames the architecture as Human Knower <-> KnowledgeOS Ātma <-> Knowledge Space, with Zero/Lord/Sārathi operating between the current state and the expanding knowledge horizon, and proposes that the next formal question should be 'what is the exact relationship between the Human Knower Ātma and the KnowledgeOS Ātma?' rather than continuing with an isolated mathematical object — called 'a significant conceptual milestone'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: N=(Identity,Intent,Perspective,Context,Goals,Capabilities,Constraints,...)
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the Knower itself as the biggest missing formally-completed piece despite 𝒜_H (Knower Ātma) being named: proposes N=(Identity,Intent,Perspective,Context,Goals,Capabilities,Constraints,...) as the needed model, motivated by the principle that two Knowers can observe the same reality and produce different Ideal States — 'not an error, a fundamental property of the system'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \widehat K_t = \text{best available reconstruction from }O_{\le t}
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes 'we try our best but never reach the best' as K̂_t = best available reconstruction from O_≤t, with K̂_t ≠ K_t possibly persisting even as observations accumulate (O_≤t1 ⊆ O_≤t2 may give a better but still imperfect K̂_t2). Draws a careful analogy to least-squares/Gaussian estimation (x̂=argmin_x‖Ax-b‖²): 'best approximation under a criterion' does not guarantee x̂=x_true, giving 'Best reconstruction under regime R ≠ complete underlying Knowledge'. Places measure/probability theory specifically at the Observations->probabilistic reconstruction step (P(K_t|F_t), E[X_t|F_t]), with K_t itself 'conceptually prior' to the probabilistic extraction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ātman should not be modeled as an "Ideal State" itself. It is better modeled as the invariant identity underlying changing states.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a proposed equation of Ātman with the Ideal State, offering instead 'Persistent Identity / Invariant Subject' ℐ with ℐ_{t+1}=ℐ_t while K_{t+1}≠K_t and I_{t+1}≠I_t in general, giving Identity ≠ Current State ≠ Ideal State — 'a very important refinement'. K_t = State(ℐ,t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_0 \subseteq? K_1 \subseteq? K_2
a_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge evolution K_0->K_1->K_2->... within K_t⊆𝒦 is NOT necessarily monotonic — an assertion can be accepted, then questioned, then rejected, so K_{t+1} may contain less information than K_t in one sense while being epistemically better, reinforcing the earlier distinction between knowledge quantity and knowledge quality/coherence. Also cautions against assuming lim_{t->∞} K_t = 𝒦 as a mathematical fact rather than an assumption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Ātman doctrine} \rightarrow \text{philosophical inspiration} \rightarrow \text{Invariant Identity abstraction}
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit philosophy/mathematics firewall: 'The Gītā teaches that Ātman is not destroyed' does NOT mathematically imply 'our model proves an invariant identity exists' — Ātman doctrine -> philosophical inspiration -> Invariant Identity abstraction, never Ātman doctrine ⇒ mathematical theorem. Recommends adding 'Persistent Identity / Invariant Subject' as a new theoretical concept (not folding Ātman into Ideal State), with a suggested documentation sentence: 'The concept of Ātman provides a philosophical analogue for the architectural concept of persistent identity... KnowledgeOS may use this as a conceptual inspiration, but does not claim to computationally model Ātman or establish its metaphysical truth.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: atman-in-the-conceptual-model -> atman-within-our-knowledgeos-theory -> atma-and-kernel-are-the-same-underlying-idea -> atma-can-be-the-knowledgeos-kernel -- fourth turning point -- a four-document escalation ending in Atma can be the Kernel ... The corpus also issues its own guard against over-literal mapping (correction-don-t-map-chakra-knowledge-layer).
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies R3's fourth turning point: a four-document escalation across 14 minutes (08-27 08:51-09:05) moving from 'Atma usable in the conceptual model' to 'Atma can be the Kernel', while also noting the corpus issued its own guard against over-literal mapping (a correction document refusing to map chakras directly onto knowledge layers) and flags that whether Atma-as-Kernel was ever tested is NOT ESTABLISHED at inventory depth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: OQ-01 What is the Kernel object, if not Knowledge? ... never answered in-corpus; R5's answer (8 primitives) is a kernel, but the R1 question was about the object of protection | OQ-03 Is Determination ... now covered by step-008 acceptance/commitment -- or still missing? R1->R5 mapping absent | OQ-05 Did Atma-as-Kernel survive? (025s mentions Knowledge Atma) R3->R5, unmapped
a_rows_sample.statement: Records three unresolved substantive questions the corpus itself never answers: OQ-01 what the Kernel object actually is if not Knowledge (R1's original object-of-protection question, distinct from R5's 8-primitive kernel answer); OQ-03 whether R1's 'Determination is the missing mathematical object' is now covered by step-008's acceptance/commitment machinery or still missing (no R1->R5 mapping exists); OQ-05 whether Atma-as-Kernel survived into R5 (a 025s document mentions 'Knowledge Atma' but the R3->R5 mapping is unestablished).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 4 ATMAN -- UNKNOWN (hypothesis without descendants) ... never tested, never withdrawn; C-012 remains OPEN. The 025s trace needs one read in Phase 2B to classify as refined or abandoned
a_rows_sample.statement: Traces Atman/Atma's lineage from R3's 14-minute escalation to 'Atma can be the KnowledgeOS Kernel' through a later trace ('Knowledge Atma' in step-025s) to absence from the final 8-primitive kernel and Steps 100-158 vocabulary -- final verdict UNKNOWN: the hypothesis was never tested nor formally withdrawn, C-012 remains OPEN, and the 025s trace needs a dedicated read to classify it as refined or abandoned.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I (calligraphic) != K_t != I_t ... Delta_t = D(K_t, I_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a three-way distinction between persistent identity of the observation/epistemic subject (calligraphic I), the actual/current knowledge state K_t, and the ideal/required knowledge state I_t, with Delta_t=D(K_t,I_t) as the knowledge gap; explicitly frames this via an Atman-inspired but strictly-bounded analogy ('Atman -> philosophical inspiration; Persistent Identity -> candidate mathematical/architectural abstraction', never 'Atman -> proof'), motivated by the concern that otherwise every changed fact (e.g. Nexus RAM 31GB->64GB) risks being interpreted as a new object rather than a state change of the same identity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity != State and Identity != Ideal State ... Does the identity of K_t remain the same when knowledge changes?
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the persistent-identity hypothesis (I_{t+1}=I_t while K_{t+1}!=K_t) as yielding two further non-collapse claims, Identity != State and Identity != Ideal State, explicitly held as a candidate abstraction not yet established by any of the three traditions, with the open research question of whether K_t's identity remains the same across knowledge change left unanswered.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'persistent-identity-of-observation-hypothesis' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledge-atma-identity-concept' (batch B0056). Note: A candidate abstraction (explicitly Atman-inspired but held as engineering hypothesis, not metaphysical proof) distinguishing three objects: persistent identity of the observation/epistemic subject (calligraphic I), current knowledge state K_t, and ideal/required state I_t; the point is that K_t1 != K_t2 (e.g. RAM changed from 31GB to 64GB) does not by itself imply the identity changed (I_t1=I_t2), guarding against every changed fact being treated as a new object; leaves open what exactly owns that identity (the observation, the knowledge object, the epistemic subject, the domain entity, the system, or an aggregate). Explicit discipline stated: 'Atman -> philosophical inspiration; Persistent Identity -> candidate mathematical/architectural abstraction', not 'Atman -> proof of Persistent Identity.' Possibly the same underlying concept as the pre-existing knowledge-atma-identity-concept (B0020's Knowledge Atma A_K), possibly an independently re-derived, not-yet-reconciled candidate -- not resolved by this batch.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1} = Learn( K_t, Observations_t, Events_t, Policies_t, Outcomes_t )... the source states the decision and world equations (A_t = Decision(K_t, S_t, Policy_t); S_{t+1} = F(S_t, A_t, U_t)), keeping three evolutions -- of knowledge, of choices, of the world -- as three different functions.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the knowledge state's time-indexed dynamics as three separate evolution functions: K_{t+1}=Learn(K_t, Observations_t, Events_t, Policies_t, Outcomes_t) for knowledge, A_t=Decision(K_t, S_t, Policy_t) for choices, and S_{t+1}=F(S_t, A_t, U_t) for the world -- kept as three distinct functions, with time-indexing meaning there is no bare "the knowledge," only knowledge-as-of-t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CORE: Entity, State, Event, Observation / EPISTEMIC: Evidence, Claim, Uncertainty / SEMANTIC:... / RELATIONAL:... / GOVERNANCE:... / OPERATIONAL:... / EVOLUTION:... Then, family by family, the source interrogates each concept -- is this primitive, or constructible? -- and most collapse... What survives... K = (E, S, T, O, P, R, Pi, A)
a_rows_sample.statement: Reproduces the source's reduction derivation from an initial seven-family stratification (Core/Epistemic/Semantic/Relational/Governance/Operational/Evolution) to the frozen eight-tuple candidate kernel K=(E,S,T,O,P,R,Pi,A) -- entities, states, temporal/event structure, observations, propositions, typed relations, policies, actions -- by showing most non-core concepts (Evidence, Claim, Identity, Provenance, Causality/Dependency, Uncertainty, Authority/Decision, Outcome, Learning/Revision/Drift) individually reduce to typed structure over the four cores plus the four surviving structure-carriers (Proposition, Relation, Policy, Action).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence = QualifiedObservation... Claim = Proposition... Identity = EntityIdentityRelation... Uncertainty = epistemic annotation U(C) (probabilistic OR not -- 49.10's Probability != EpistemicConfidence)... Authority = governance structure over decisions (Authority(actor, d))... resist inventing primitives -- the reduction's whole yield is that richer notions are TYPED STRUCTURE
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists the derived-structure layer -- the equations by which richer concepts are expressed as typed structure over the eight primitives rather than as new primitives themselves (Evidence=QualifiedObservation; Claim=Proposition; Identity=EntityIdentityRelation; Provenance=TypedDependencyRelation; Uncertainty=epistemic annotation U(C), explicitly not assumed probabilistic -- Probability != EpistemicConfidence; Authority=governance structure over decisions; Decision=structure over K,S,Policy with Proposal kept distinct from AuthorizedDecision; Outcome=observed consequence of Action; Learning/Revision/Drift=evolution structure) and states the modelling discipline this yields: resist inventing new primitives, since typed structure can be checked/queried/governed in ways ad-hoc primitives cannot.

a_rows_sample.anchor: stress-tested by twelve falsification experiments (49.78-49.89... What the argument does not and cannot claim, and the source itself refuses to claim: completeness... minimality... and uniqueness... The source's own word is the governing one: a candidate mathematical kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Teaches PF-2 in place at its exact strength: the eight-primitive reduction argument is RECONSTRUCTABLE, stress-tested by twelve falsification experiments (each attempting to express a rich concept in Structure(primitives) and failing the kernel if it cannot be done) plus Step 050's fifty-attack consistency audit; but completeness (no needed concept will ever fail to reduce), minimality (no seven-element basis would suffice -- the source concedes Entity is "arguably" Identity+State, kept for DDD-pragmatic reasons), and uniqueness (no alternative basis exists) remain explicitly NOT ESTABLISHED, matching the source's own characterization of it as a "candidate" kernel and a design result, not a theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Collapse the typed relation set into a single generic RelatedTo(A, B) and semantics die: an AI consumer, seeing RelatedTo everywhere, infers RelatedTo => Causes -- recreating "one of the fundamental problems we eliminated in Step 43." One typed set, seven meanings; one generic edge, license to hallucinate causality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reproduces the source's own worked failure case for mis-typing the Relation primitive: collapsing the seven typed relations (Supports, DependsOn, Causes, Identifies, MapsTo, Contradicts, Precedes) into a single generic RelatedTo(A,B) edge causes an AI consumer to infer RelatedTo implies Causes, recreating a causal-hallucination failure mode the architecture had previously eliminated; extended to the election running example (DerivedFrom(wireSummary,wireReport) and Supports blurred into RelatedTo would let a derived summary quietly become a second independent witness) as the same dependency failure seen at the primitive-typing layer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K-1 K_t over 8 primitives ... RATIFIED -- '50 attack classes, no counterexample', COMPUTATIONALLY TESTED ... [NEG] 'Four rival K vocabularies' is WITHDRAWN. K_t is RATIFIED. (A,R) is a projection of it, not an alternative.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 5: re-audits the seven 'rival K vocabularies' (K-1 through K-7 plus Theory 01's separately-scoped carrier) and reclassifies all as projection/refinement/superseded/rejected/intentionally-different-context, finding no category-G (genuinely incompatible) member, withdrawing the prior 'four rival K vocabularies' framing; per the document's own self-declared status, K-1 (K_t over 8 primitives {Entity,State,Event,Observation,Proposition,Relation,Policy,Action}) is claimed RATIFIED and COMPUTATIONALLY TESTED, (A,R) is claimed as a lossy semantic projection pi_K(K_t) rather than a rival; what the document says genuinely survives is narrower: K-CANONICAL-DECISION is prepared but not taken, K_core (the operational kernel) is not determined (canonical state relationship established =/= canonical operational kernel established), pi_K is not computable (blocked by Qualify) so observational equivalence is refuted, and the 8 ratified primitives have never been shown minimal against an operation space.

a_aliases: The Knowledge State and Its Eight Primitives (book III.3)

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'K_t'

a_rows_sample.anchor: At least the following relations must be separated: = representation/structural equality; ≡ semantic equality; ≈ observational equivalence; ≅_I identity equivalence; ≅_P provenance-sensitive equivalence; ≅_H historical equivalence.
a_rows_sample.statement: The overloaded notation K1=K2 is decomposed into (at least) six distinct relations that must not be conflated: structural equality (=), semantic equality (equiv), observational equivalence (approx), identity equivalence (cong_I), provenance-sensitive equivalence (cong_P), and historical equivalence (cong_H); the corpus is said to explicitly record the first four distinctions and warn they are not interchangeable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Same proposition ⇏ Same evidence identity. ... two observations can concern the same proposition while remaining distinct evidence objects.
a_rows_sample.statement: Preserved historical result: identity is not equality — two evidence objects e1,e2 can both support the same proposition p (Supports(e1,p) and Supports(e2,p)) without e1=e2; this affects provenance, deduplication, replay, validation, audit and merge, and is attributed to an earlier corpus reconstruction rather than newly derived here.

a_rows_sample.anchor: x =_str y iff their representations are structurally identical. ... =_str ≠ semantic equality unless the representation has already been proven canonical.
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural equality x=_str y (representations structurally identical) is computationally convenient but is warned to not equal semantic equality unless the representation is already proven canonical — two structurally different representations can denote the same semantic state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: x ≡_sem y iff Semantics(x)=Semantics(y). ... Semantic equality is conceptually appropriate, but currently underdefined.
a_rows_sample.statement: Semantic equality x equiv_sem y is defined via a semantic interpretation function Sem:Representation->Meaning being equal on x and y, but is flagged as not computationally decidable while Sem itself remains formally undefined — conceptually appropriate but currently underdefined.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H1 ≈ H2 iff every permitted observation produces the same result: ∀O∈𝒪: O(H1)=O(H2). ... This is the relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient.
a_rows_sample.statement: Observational equivalence for histories (H1 approx H2 iff every permitted observation O produces the same result) and for states (K1 approx K2 iff every permitted state observation agrees) is identified as the same relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient; notably it does not require internal representations to be identical.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SameId(x,y) ... Identity tracks denotation; equality compares values. This formulation is a reconstruction, not yet a corpus-proven final definition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identity (SameId(x,y)) answers whether two references denote the same domain object, independent of value equality: x=_str y can hold with SameId false (two separately created records with identical content but distinct observations), and SameId can hold while representations differ (the same domain object having evolved) — 'identity tracks denotation; equality compares values', explicitly flagged as a reconstruction, not a corpus-proven final definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Historical equality asks: Are these states the same point or condition in an evolution history? ... Semantic equality ⇏ Historical equality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Historical equality asks whether two states are the same point in an evolution history, distinct from current semantic equality: K0 -Revise-> K1 can have K0 equiv_sem K1 (representation changed, semantics didn't) while K0 !=_H K1 (distinct historical states) — semantic equality does not imply historical equality; matters especially for Replay and audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance is semantically relevant: K1 ≢ K2. Provenance is metadata only: K1 ≡ K2. ... equality cannot be resolved until the theory determines which information is semantically essential. This is a key dependency for Step 265.
a_rows_sample.statement: Provenance equality is genuinely ambiguous: given K1={p,e1}, K2={p,e2} with e1!=e2 both supporting p, either provenance is semantically relevant (K1 not-equiv K2) or metadata only (K1 equiv K2); the earlier corpus is said to identify this ambiguity explicitly and conclude it cannot be resolved until the theory determines which information is semantically essential — flagged as a key dependency for Step 265 (provenance placement).

a_rows_sample.anchor: No universal equality hierarchy has yet been proven. ... Identity and Provenance equality are independent dimensions.
a_rows_sample.statement: A candidate implication chain (structural => semantic => observational equivalence) is proposed but explicitly not declared universally valid without further assumptions; identity and provenance equality are treated as independent dimensions from this chain; current position: no universal equality hierarchy has yet been proven.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Explicit assertion membership ≠ semantic entailment. ... a∈_exp K ... K⊨a ... Stored fact ≠ logically derived fact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Membership in an assertion-based state K is typed into explicit assertion membership (a in_exp K, a is literally one of K's stored assertions) versus semantic consequence (K models a, semantically entailed but not necessarily stored) — a proposed formal distinction (not yet a theorem) preventing the category error of treating a stored fact as identical to a logically derived one; flagged as essential for Step 262's assertion type.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Merge equality: semantic + identity + provenance dependent. Exact final semantics remain unresolved.
a_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Merge: Merge(K1,K2) cannot be specified using structural equality alone, since a1=(p,e1) and a2=(p,e2) sharing proposition p could legitimately merge to {a1,a2} (kept separate) or to a single combined-evidence assertion depending on ontology; Merge equality is semantic+identity+provenance dependent, with exact final semantics unresolved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Supersession requires identity/version distinction. ... collapsing them under semantic equality would destroy the very relation x2 ≻ x1.
a_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Supersede: if Meaning(x1)=Meaning(x2) but Identity(x1)!=Identity(x2) and x2 supersedes x1, collapsing x1,x2 under semantic equality would destroy the supersession relation x2 succ x1 itself; supersession therefore requires an identity/version distinction, strongly suggesting semantic equality alone cannot serve as the sole equality relation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Replay requires historical identity/equality independent of current state equality. ... Replay(H1)=K and Replay(H2)=K yet H1 ≠_H H2.
a_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Replay: two distinct histories H1,H2 (H1 !=_H H2) can replay to the same current state K (Replay(H1)=Replay(H2)=K); Replay is treated by the corpus as a history/audit operation rather than another state transformation, and requires historical identity/equality independent of current-state equality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Operation | Structural equality | Semantic equality | Identity | Historical equality | Provenance | Current assessment | Merge...Supersede...Replay...Remove...Revise...Deduplicate...Validate
a_rows_sample.statement: The full operation/equality matrix across Merge, Supersede, Replay, Remove, Revise, Deduplicate, Validate rates each of structural/semantic/identity/historical/provenance equality as insufficient, required, relevant, potentially-required, or context-dependent per operation, with every row's overall status UNRESOLVED, NORMATIVE/DOMAIN-DEPENDENT (Deduplicate), or 'Assessment relation' (Validate); Remove requires identity for correct object targeting (must not remove a2 when removing a1 despite structural identity), Revise cannot use semantic equality as its sole target selector (must not implicitly revise x2 when revising x1 despite x1 equiv_sem x2), Deduplicate cannot be specified until its preservation policy is known (structural/semantic/identity/provenance criteria can each give different results), and Validate shows semantic state equality does not imply identical validation results because validation is a relation over (K,E) pairs, not K alone — reinforcing that not every operation is a state transformation T:K->K.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No single equality relation is adequate for all KnowledgeOS operations. ... KnowledgeOS requires a typed family of relations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Major correction to the kernel concept: rejects the implicit assumption 'KnowledgeOS needs one equality operator', replacing it with 'KnowledgeOS requires a typed family of relations' (=_str, equiv_sem, approx_obs, SameId, equiv_H, equiv_P) that may be connected by formally established implications but must not be conflated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K1 ≡_K K2 ⟺ ∀O∈𝒪_K: O(K1)=O(K2) ... 𝒪_K is not yet completely closed. Therefore this is a candidate formal definition, not a completed theorem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate formal definition of Knowledge-State equality as purely observational/behavioral: K1 equiv_K K2 iff every permitted state observation O in the (not-yet-closed) set O_K agrees on K1 and K2; explicitly a candidate, not a completed theorem, because O_K is not yet closed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Equality → Congruence → Quotient → Minimality. This is the correct dependency direction.
a_rows_sample.statement: If K1 equiv_K K2 (no permitted observation distinguishes them) and all mandatory operations preserve that equivalence, equiv_K becomes the congruence relation needed for the minimal quotient K*=H/equiv (Step 260) — establishing the dependency direction Equality -> Congruence -> Quotient -> Minimality as correct.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the observation set is not fully closed; the operation registry is not fully closed; provenance placement remains unresolved; assertion semantics remain unresolved; temporal semantics remain unresolved; identity semantics remain unresolved. The governing prompt explicitly says that final kernel sele
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit refusal to overclaim equiv_K as final: six named open dependencies remain (observation-set closure, operation-registry closure, provenance placement, assertion semantics, temporal semantics, identity semantics); the governing prompt is cited as requiring final kernel selection to halt while equality remains ambiguous, and this gate is obeyed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: bounded contexts may legitimately require different relations: same assertion / same evidence / same domain identity / same version / same semantic meaning / same observable state ... PRIMARY KEY must therefore not automatically be interpreted as SemanticIdentity. ... content hash must not automatic
a_rows_sample.statement: DDD interpretation: rather than one generic 'Equality' concept used everywhere, different bounded contexts legitimately require different named relations (same assertion, same evidence, same domain identity, same version, same semantic meaning, same observable state); a database PRIMARY KEY must not automatically be interpreted as SemanticIdentity, and a content hash must not automatically become DomainIdentity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 𝔎=(K,=_str,≡_sem,≈_obs,SameId,≡_H,≡_P). The next question is not 'Which one is the equality?' It is 'Which relation is the appropriate congruence relation for each operation and which relation defines semantic equality of Knowledge States?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical reframing: KnowledgeOS's state carries a relational structure 𝔎=(K,=_str,equiv_sem,approx_obs,SameId,equiv_H,equiv_P) rather than a single equality; the research question shifts from 'which relation is THE equality' to 'which relation is the appropriate congruence for each operation, and which defines semantic equality of Knowledge States'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The reviewer proposes a "Provenance Domain" ... Verdict: PROVENANCE is not a missing domain — it is a DISPERSED, NAMED, PARTLY-GOVERNED concern
b_rows_sample.statement: A check-before-recording pass finds provenance already lives in the corpus as: one axis of AUTHORITY itself (provenance x standing, Engineering Progression Model, PM-1), the PROVENANCE non-progression kind, identity discipline (CAP-001), evidence grading practice ([FETCHED]/[CANONICAL]/[2nd-hand]), and append-only evidence/traceability blocks. Verdict: provenance is a dispersed, named, partly-governed concern (the SP-5 pattern recognized a third time), not a missing domain. Disposition: the provenance questions enrich the existing Tier-1 Knowledge Governance stream (PM-1); 'Provenance as a strategic domain' is recorded as a hypothesis routed to the docket, admissible only if a live stream produces evidence requiring it; the identity-chain observation (CAP-001 as foundation if provenance grows) is a watch item, not a promotion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U-GR-2 | Provenance: enrichment of Knowledge Governance (current disposition) or eventually its own domain?
b_rows_sample.statement: U-GR-2: whether provenance remains an enrichment of Knowledge Governance or eventually becomes its own domain, waiting on operational evidence from the live streams, not literature.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PM-1 ENRICHED (2026-08-03, external input): PROVENANCE as a named first-class concern
b_rows_sample.statement: PM-1 (provenance x standing) is enriched: industry treats provenance as a governance control plane (identity -> version -> retrieval event -> evidence -> answer -> audit), paralleling P4 and resting on identity discipline (CAP-001). Provenance already lives dispersed in the corpus (authority axis, non-progression kind, evidence grading, traceability blocks); 'Provenance as its own domain' is a hypothesis at the docket, not a new backlog stream — this row owns the questions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: authority = provenance × standing ... [CANONICAL] W3C PROV: derivation is an immutable provenance fact
b_rows_sample.statement: The formula authority = provenance x standing is supported by W3C PROV (derivation is an immutable provenance fact) and data-catalog practice (lineage != 'certified' flag are two independent fields in every major catalog). No challenge. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SC-5 | authority = provenance × standing in ONE field (its own header asks two questions)
b_rows_sample.statement: SC-5: authority combines provenance and standing into one field, though its own header asks two separate questions; open, routed to PM-1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED IN FULL — AND IT IS MY FOURTH INSTANCE OF LEVEL CONFUSION ... I-4 is NOT falsified. I misdiagnosed a LIFECYCLE gap as an ONTOLOGY falsification
b_rows_sample.statement: A prior claim that I-4 was falsified is retracted: a discharge summary is not authoritative because it was projected, but became authoritative through DERIVED -> REVIEWED -> ATTESTED -> RELEASED; governance created the authority, not the derivation. The corrected conclusion is not 'DP-2 is wrong' but 'DP-2 conflates DERIVATION with ATTESTATION'. Four prior level confusions listed: flat vs dimensional (taxonomy), artifact vs concept (existence), layer vs sibling (ontology), lifecycle vs structure (this one). A fifth was avoided by checking: the author was about to report 'there is no lifecycle', when in fact nine exist.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The precise gap — located mechanically ... THE GAP: STATUS HAS A GOVERNED STATE MACHINE. AUTHORITY DOES NOT
b_rows_sample.statement: statuses.yaml and authorities.yaml are declared orthogonal but are not equally equipped: statuses.yaml has 8 values, a progression field (order), a terminal marker (settled), a defined who-may-move role table, and lint-checkable transition guards; authorities.yaml has 5 values and none of these. Authority gates a status transition, but nothing governs how authority itself changes — no rule for who may move derived->authoritative, and no guard for it. This is exactly the I-4 problem: attestation is an authority transition (derived->authoritative); because authority transitions are ungoverned, the model cannot express 'attested', so it collapses derived into 'never authoritative'. A prior reviewer's diagnosis ('DP-2 conflates derivation and attestation') now has a mechanical cause.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LG-1 (WITHDRAWN 2026-08-02 — ILL-POSED) ... authority is TWO dimensions in one field — immutable PROVENANCE × act-changed STANDING
b_rows_sample.statement: LG-1 ('should authority have a governed state machine?') is withdrawn as ill-posed: the question dissolved under discovery that authority is two dimensions in one field — immutable PROVENANCE (generated, derived) times act-changed STANDING (authoritative, provisional, historical). Provenance cannot have a state machine; standing changes by governance acts. Superseded by PM-1/PM-2, recorded in the Engineering Progression Model section 4.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LG-2 | Restate DP-2 to separate DERIVATION from ATTESTATION?
b_rows_sample.statement: LG-2: should DP-2 be restated to separate DERIVATION from ATTESTATION — this is CV-1, now with a mechanical cause; routed to the ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 2. CANDIDATE — supported by evidence, awaiting ruling or more evidence (K-1..K-15)
b_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Convergences — conclusions this track reached that the blind review reproduced (items 1-12)
b_rows_sample.statement: Twelve conclusions reproduced blind, now carrying double independent derivation: (1) KnowledgeOS is a hypothesis, gate shut, Vision unapproved; (2) 'PublicDigit is the laboratory' rejected against ADR-AIP-02, Product Primacy governs; (3) the EKP is a real governed context with named individual owner; (4) Engineering Governance is the strongest bounded context; (5) the reusable kernel list, near-identical; (6) designed-for-reuse != demonstrated-reusable (verbatim convergence); (7) individual EKP ownership is a succession risk, sharpened to 'separation of duties is real as process and unevidenced as people'; (8) three knowledge ontologies coexist unreconciled; (9) domain-free methodology sits in product paths, placement breached, plus a new instance (Platform_Capability_Pattern); (10) PMR-10's manual adoption failed, sharpened into a falsification of the Reference Architecture's protocol-suffices stance; (11) most of the 11 invariants reproduced with citations, with I-8 downgraded to invariant-in-waiting; (12) the split verdict itself (enacted internal mission vs unratified product vision).

b_rows_sample.anchor: TWO CONCESSIONS BEFORE THE MODEL ... INTENDED is WITHDRAWN as a fourth evidence grade ... Intent is not evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: A prior 'INTENDED' evidence grade is withdrawn: intent is not evidence, and applying the repository's own rule (determine whether a proposal is a new dimension, an overloaded existing dimension, or merely another value) shows INTENDED was an overloaded existing dimension, added inside a document about evidence discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The four concerns, separated as required ... A fifth concern the repository already separates ... TRUST/PROVENANCE = authorities.yaml
b_rows_sample.statement: Four concerns mapped to dimensions: EVIDENCE (D-V, new), GOVERNANCE (D-III, existing/executable via statuses.yaml), OPERATIONAL STATE (D-VI, new), INTENT (derived: f(GOVERNANCE-STATUS, OWNER), both fields already exist). A fifth concern the repository already separates, worth naming so it is not re-added later: TRUST/PROVENANCE = authorities.yaml (authoritative, derived, generated, historical, provisional), and statuses.yaml already declares status independent of authority — the repository was doing orthogonal dimensions before this commission asked for them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LG-1 was solution design, conceded ... exactly what DDD forbids. I located an asymmetry and immediately proposed its repair
b_rows_sample.statement: LG-1 ('missing transitions -> need a state machine') is conceded as solution design: an inference from a missing implementation to a model, which DDD forbids — an asymmetry was located and its repair immediately proposed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The reviewer's "that chain is QUALIFICATION, not authority" — CONFIRMED by the repository ... DERIVED → REVIEWED → ATTESTED → RELEASED describes a document becoming more trustworthy
b_rows_sample.statement: A reviewer's claim that the DERIVED->REVIEWED->ATTESTED->RELEASED chain describes qualification, not authority, is confirmed: the repository already has vocabulary for it (ES-006.1's qualification stage, ES-003 Qualification), though 'Qualification' also carries a recorded UL collision (verification activity vs promotion-ladder stage), now with a third candidate sense (the standing-assignment chain).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The progression mechanisms — inventoried as evidence (P-1..P-10)
b_rows_sample.statement: Ten progression mechanisms inventoried as observations, not assumed lifecycles: P-1 document status (8 values, order+settled+roles+guards); P-2 Authority (5 values with rank, no order/roles/guards); P-3 ES-006.1 promotion ladder; P-4 Methodology maturity; P-5 ADR-M status; P-6 Capability lifecycle; P-7 EEP (plan->...->decide); P-8 Observation Protocol (ACTIVE->CONCLUDED); P-9 Identifier lifecycles (4 series); P-10 Evidence accumulation (n=0->n=1->n>=2). A prior canonical distinction (Reference Model section 6, GEP-F1: two lifecycles never conflated, governance-artifact vs governed-work) is found before theorizing; this discovery extends that refusal rather than founding it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The flagship finding — authority is not one dimension ... authorities.yaml's own header asks TWO questions in ONE field: "how much should I trust this and where did it come from?"
b_rows_sample.statement: authorities.yaml's five values answer two different questions: 'generated' and 'derived' answer provenance (where did it come from), and can never change (origin is an immutable historical fact); 'authoritative', 'provisional', and 'historical' answer standing (how much should I trust it), and can change by a governance act. This dissolves LG-1 ('should authority have a governed state machine?') rather than answering it: half of authority cannot have a state machine (provenance never changes) and the other half changes by governance acts recorded as act-logs, not workflows. Authority = an immutable PROVENANCE fact x a mutable STANDING judgment; attestation changes standing, nothing changes provenance. This also explains why the I-4 confusion was persistent: 'derived' (provenance) was wrongly read as entailing low standing, but a signed financial statement can be derived in provenance and authoritative in standing simultaneously.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PM-1 | Should authority's two questions — provenance and standing — be separated?
b_rows_sample.statement: PM-1: should authority's two questions, provenance and standing, be separated — this supersedes LG-1, which is withdrawn as ill-posed — authority: ARB + PD-3's owner.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PM-2 | Should standing-changes (attestation, supersession) get the role/guard treatment status-changes have?
b_rows_sample.statement: PM-2: should standing-changes get the role/guard treatment status-changes have — an act-governance question, not a state-machine question — authority: ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant relationships vs implementation choices ... I-1..I-11 ... 11 invariants · 8 choices
b_rows_sample.statement: Eleven invariants traced to governed statements: I-1 Knowledge is represented by an Artifact, an Artifact is never the Knowledge; I-2 a Capability protects exactly one invariant; I-3 a Knowledge Space has a declared boundary; I-4 (underspecified, not false — holds until attestation, reclassified as a lifecycle gap not an ontology falsification, per DP-2's conflation of derivation with attestation); I-5 one authoritative artifact per topic+context (lint-enforced); I-6 the Runtime never owns Knowledge; I-7 a PKS never contains reusable Method (stated and breached); I-8 governance precedes automation; I-9 governance-status orthogonal to authority; I-10 a constitutional principle is void-overriding; I-11 (restated 2026-08-02: Knowledge does not execute, capabilities execute, knowledge constrains and informs generation — the restatement survived cross-product projection where the original would have failed). Eight implementation choices (folder mapping, markdown as representation, YAML/Mermaid, the graph's declared scope, Claude Code as the n=1 runtime adapter, frontmatter, identifier formats, Mermaid+markdown projections) may change freely without breaking the model — that distinction is what makes this a platform rather than a repository layout.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not a knowledge repository. It is not a search system. It is not an AI oracle. It is a constitutional epistemic system that protects and improves the process by which justified knowledge emerges.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines KnowledgeOS's character negatively (not a repository/search system/AI oracle) and positively as a constitutional epistemic system that protects and improves the process by which justified knowledge emerges.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge dimensions must evolve independently unless an explicit transformation connects them.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a 'dimension purity' law: Evidence changing does not automatically change Authority; Confidence increasing does not mean Truth increases; AI-generated text is not Observation; Decision is not Knowledge. KnowledgeOS prevents dimension collapse.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS = Memory of reasoning ... not only: Memory of information. It preserves the path to knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeOS is framed as a 'reasoning memory' that preserves why, from where, using what evidence, with what assumptions, under which context, at what time, and through what reasoning a conclusion was reached -- not only the conclusion itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown | Observation | Evidence | Hypothesis | Reasoning | Assessment | Validated Knowledge | Revision | New Understanding. The old state is not deleted. It becomes history.
a_rows_sample.statement: Describes an epistemic lifecycle stage sequence (Unknown->Observation->Evidence->Hypothesis->Reasoning->Assessment->Validated Knowledge->Revision->New Understanding) and asserts the old state is never deleted, only historicized.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The first state is: 'I do not yet know.' This is not weakness. It is epistemic honesty.
a_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge begins from a neutral 'Unknown' state rather than an assumed-true state, credited to 'the Zero principle'; framed as epistemic honesty rather than weakness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The system records: CONFLICTED instead of forcing: TRUE / FALSE prematurely.
a_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a normal database ('which value is correct?') with KnowledgeOS ('why do different perspectives disagree?'): Claim A + Evidence A and Claim B + Evidence B may coexist as CONFLICTED rather than forcing a premature TRUE/FALSE resolution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A conclusion must never become an observation. Especially: AI generated answer != Fact from reality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Observed reality -> Evidence -> Reasoning -> Conclusion are different epistemic categories; a conclusion must never become an observation, and an AI-generated answer must never be treated as a fact from reality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Meaning + Context = Knowledge. Removing context destroys knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Meaning does not exist independently of context (example: 'The system is cold' could mean a temperature problem, unfriendly behavior, or a market slowdown); Meaning + Context = Knowledge, and removing context destroys knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: But: Revision != Deletion. The historical reasoning remains.
a_rows_sample.statement: A truth-seeking system must allow itself to be wrong: accepted knowledge can be revised in light of new evidence, but revision is never deletion -- historical reasoning remains.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge -> Assessment -> Decision -> Action. The system preserves: 'Why was this action justified at that time?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge does not directly execute; it flows through Assessment and Decision before Action, and the system preserves why an action was justified at the time it was taken.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mathematics describes the structure. It does not create the structure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Topology (invariants/transformations), lattices (partial ordering), temporal logic (validity over time), graphs (relationships), and sheaf-like thinking (local/global consistency) are useful as descriptive tools; claims like 'KnowledgeOS is a complex number' or 'is a formula' are rejected -- mathematics describes structure, it does not define it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If KnowledgeOS were a person, it would be: A careful scientist + historian + judge ... Philosopher ... Engineer
a_rows_sample.statement: Personifies KnowledgeOS's character as a composite: Scientist ('what evidence supports this?'), Historian ('how did this belief evolve?'), Judge ('what authority process justified this?'), Philosopher ('what does this actually mean?'), Engineer ('can this transformation happen safely?').

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a constitutional epistemic system designed to preserve the integrity of knowledge evolution... It does not manufacture truth; it creates the conditions where trustworthy truth can emerge, survive transformation, and improve through continuous reasoning and revision.
a_rows_sample.statement: First 'Final Character Statement': KnowledgeOS preserves the integrity of knowledge evolution by maintaining separation between meaning, evidence, authority, context, time, reasoning, and action; it creates conditions for trustworthy truth rather than manufacturing truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A KnowledgeOS kernel is not a container for knowledge. It is a protector of the relationships that make knowledge trustworthy... KnowledgeOS protects the path from observation to justified understanding.
a_rows_sample.statement: A second, shorter essence statement: the kernel is a protector of relationships that make knowledge trustworthy, and it protects the path from observation to justified understanding.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. What exists? ... 2. Why should we believe it? ... 3. Who produced this understanding? ... 4. How does it change? ... 5. What can be done with it?
a_rows_sample.statement: Restructures the character model into five constitutional questions, each preserving a dimension group: Identity (semantic identity/context/meaning/lineage), Evidence/Justification (observations/evidence/reasoning/contradictions/assumptions), Epistemic Agency (observer/analyst/reasoner/validator/authority source), Transformation/Time (evolution/revisions/supersession/historical states), Decision Relationship (decisions influenced/actions justified/consequences).

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is the constitutional epistemic substrate that preserves the integrity of the relationship between the Knower, the Known, the Evidence, and the transformations through which justified understanding evolves over time.
a_rows_sample.statement: A refined one-sentence essence statement, explicitly offered as an improvement over a prior version that named only 'the Knower, the Known, and the Path of Reasoning'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would not say 'the kernel is ready to be written in stone.' ... Research insight -> Candidate invariant -> Cross-domain validation -> Established invariant -> Kernel law ... Kernel laws are not yet finalized.
a_rows_sample.statement: Cautions against prematurely declaring the kernel finalized: the discovery phase produced a strong candidate model, but the established discipline requires research insight to pass through candidate-invariant, cross-domain-validation, and established-invariant stages before becoming kernel law; status recorded as character definition/invariant candidates/kernel boundary/research lenses all 'mature' but kernel laws explicitly 'not yet finalized'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the new entries should enter as: INV-KOS-Agent-001 — Candidate, INV-KOS-Decision-001 — Candidate, INV-KOS-Revisability-001 — Candidate, INV-KOS-Inference-001 — Candidate, INV-KOS-Justification-001 — Candidate
a_rows_sample.statement: Names five candidate invariants queued for a 'KnowledgeOS Constitutional Invariant Map v1.0'; only INV-KOS-Agent-001 is defined in this file, the other four (Decision-001, Revisability-001, Inference-001, Justification-001) are named without content.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Before Tarka: KnowledgeOS preserves trustworthy knowledge evolution. After Tarka: KnowledgeOS preserves the conditions under which reasoning can transform evidence into trustworthy knowledge... Tarka explains that the middle part cannot be a black box.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the character statement to foreground reasoning as the (previously implicit, black-boxed) middle step between Evidence and Knowledge conclusion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reasoning is a governed transformation ... Input: Evidence + Context + Existing Knowledge -> Transformation: Reasoning Process -> Output: Derived Knowledge State. Not: Evidence -> Magic AI -> Truth.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a new principle: KnowledgeOS must treat reasoning as a governed transformation with explicit inputs (evidence, context, existing knowledge) and outputs (derived knowledge state), explicitly rejecting an opaque 'Evidence -> Magic AI -> Truth' model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model | 5 independent converging passes | Candidate
b_rows_sample.statement: The dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model is held as a Candidate architectural hypothesis, supported by 5 independent converging passes; movement requires an MM-1 ruling and D-8 reconciliation, decided by the ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This projection decides nothing and is authoritative for nothing
b_rows_sample.statement: The dashboard is explicitly non-authoritative and non-deciding: it exists only so humans can see, on one page, what architectural hypotheses are being tested and what evidence would count as a result; rows change only on evidence or an authority ruling, never on a schedule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is not a KnowledgeOS architecture proposal. ... EXTERNAL RESEARCH ≠ KNOWLEDGEOS ARCHITECTURE
b_rows_sample.statement: The document repeatedly and explicitly frames itself as an independent external-research evidence base for later comparison against reconstructed EKS/PKS/AIP architectures, and NOT itself a KnowledgeOS architecture proposal; the closing discipline statement instructs: do not design the kernel, do not choose technology, do not define bounded contexts, do not create ADRs, do not propose migration -- 'the output is an independent research evidence base for a later architecture decision.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge often crosses organizational boundaries. Therefore strict bounded contexts may fragment knowledge unnecessarily. ... DDD is less clearly validated as a universal organizing principle for knowledge representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD concepts (ownership, invariants, policies, language) help model knowledge-system governance, but evidence is mixed on DDD as a universal organizing principle for knowledge representation, because knowledge often crosses organizational boundaries and strict bounded contexts may fragment it unnecessarily.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There is no established academic architecture pattern known as a 'Knowledge Operating System.' ... KnowledgeOS is not entering an established category.
b_rows_sample.statement: Direct research into 'Knowledge Operating System' terminology finds only vendor marketing, AI-memory platforms, experimental open-source projects, and personal knowledge tools; there is no established academic architecture pattern by this name, and the term is currently emerging, inconsistent, and frequently marketing-driven -- therefore KnowledgeOS (this project) is not entering an established research category.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No mature research field appears to define a universally accepted: knowledge kernel, epistemic kernel, organizational memory kernel ... The term exists mostly as metaphor, prototype vocabulary, or isolated conceptual work.
b_rows_sample.statement: Direct research finding: no mature research field defines a universally accepted 'knowledge kernel', 'epistemic kernel', or 'organizational memory kernel' -- the term exists mostly as metaphor, prototype vocabulary, or isolated conceptual work; this is recorded as a research gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Research on operating systems repeatedly emphasizes: stable primitives, minimal trusted core, separation of mechanism and policy, composability ... Knowledge systems lack: deterministic execution, strict process isolation, universal semantics ... OS analogies are useful heuristics, not architectural proofs.
b_rows_sample.statement: The Unix/Linux analogy is architecturally useful for stable primitives, a minimal trusted core, mechanism/policy separation, and composability, but knowledge systems lack the deterministic execution, strict process isolation, and universal semantics of operating systems -- OS analogies are 'useful heuristics, not architectural proofs.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Successful ecosystems often separate: core standards, extensibility mechanisms, commercial capabilities. Governance and interoperability matter more than licensing for architecture.
b_rows_sample.statement: Comparative research on open-source vs commercial architecture finds that successful ecosystems separate core standards, extensibility mechanisms, and commercial capabilities, and that governance and interoperability matter more than licensing model for architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Debate | Position A | Position B ... Knowledge structure Graph/Documents ... History Events/State+history ... No universal winner exists. Context determines suitability.
b_rows_sample.statement: The literature contains unresolved cross-research contradictions with no universal winner: Knowledge structure (Graph vs Documents), History (Events vs State+history), Semantics (Ontology-first vs Emergent), Governance (Strong approval vs Collaborative editing), Consistency (Deterministic vs Probabilistic), Memory (Centralized vs Federated), AI (AI-centric vs Human-centric); context determines suitability in each case.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The literature remains weak regarding: organizational epistemic kernels, authority modeling as a distinct primitive, institutional memory architectures, long-horizon decision lineage, provenance-aware AI governance, knowledge operating systems as a formal discipline
b_rows_sample.statement: Six research gaps are recorded: organizational epistemic kernels, authority modeling as a distinct primitive, institutional memory architectures, long-horizon decision lineage, provenance-aware AI governance, and knowledge operating systems as a formal discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No conclusion can yet be drawn regarding: kernel structure, domain model, bounded contexts, storage architecture, graph centrality, event sourcing, AI integration. Those remain comparison questions.
b_rows_sample.statement: The document explicitly refuses to draw conclusions about kernel structure, domain model, bounded contexts, storage architecture, graph centrality, event sourcing, or AI integration for KnowledgeOS -- these are labelled comparison questions to be resolved only against reconstructed EKS/PKS/AIP evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Those are excellent research candidates, but we must now label them: EXTERNAL RESEARCH CANDIDATE ↓ NOT YET ↓ KnowledgeOS kernel candidate
b_rows_sample.statement: Commentary pass proposes a mandatory classification-layer discipline when consuming the external research's 'Smallest Trustworthy Core' list: every candidate must be explicitly labelled EXTERNAL RESEARCH CANDIDATE -> NOT YET -> KnowledgeOS kernel candidate, because the source research itself says these must still be compared with EKS/PKS/AIP.

b_rows_sample.anchor: So now we have three evidence layers ... CURRENT SYSTEMS / EXTERNAL RESEARCH / INTERNAL HYPOTHESES ... CROSS-SYSTEM COMPARISON ↓ DDD VALIDATION ↓ KERNEL CANDIDATES ↓ HUMAN ARCHITECTURE DECISION
b_rows_sample.statement: Commentary pass proposes a three-evidence-layer investigation model (Current Systems=EKS/PKS/AIP; External Research=KMS/AKM/PROV/epistemic systems/organizational memory/temporal systems; Internal Hypotheses=brainstorming corpus) feeding a pipeline of Cross-System Comparison -> DDD Validation -> Kernel Candidates -> Human Architecture Decision, and recommends stopping broad external-research collection in favour of the comparison phase.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Which of these externally validated principles are already embodied in EKS, PKS, or AIP, which are missing, which are duplicated, and which would actually require a new KnowledgeOS kernel boundary?'
b_rows_sample.statement: The commentary pass reframes the driving research question from 'What should a KnowledgeOS kernel contain?' to 'Which of these externally validated principles are already embodied in EKS, PKS, or AIP, which are missing, which are duplicated, and which would actually require a new KnowledgeOS kernel boundary?' -- framed as the investigation that determines whether any kernel is a real extraction from the existing ecosystem rather than an invented new system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The term 'Knowledge Operating System' appears primarily in industry/marketing contexts ... a LinkedIn article (2026) describes a 'Knowledge Operating System' as treating organizational knowledge as governed infrastructure, compiling knowledge into a persistent wiki, versioned, auditable, access-controlled.
b_rows_sample.statement: Second-pass draft adds a dedicated 'Knowledge Operating System terminology' section (not present as a distinct section in pass 1): the term appears in a 2026 LinkedIn article describing a KOS as governed infrastructure compiled into a persistent, versioned, auditable, access-controlled wiki, but no peer-reviewed literature establishes 'Knowledge OS' as a canonical architecture pattern; related terms ('knowledge infrastructure', 'knowledge runtime', 'knowledge kernel') appear sporadically without established definitions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: They are not two independent architectural authorities. They overlap heavily: Research 1 + Research 2 ↓ External Research Corpus ↓ Research-supported hypotheses
b_rows_sample.statement: Final commentary pass instructs that the two research drafts must be treated as one combined external research corpus rather than two independent architectural authorities, since they overlap heavily and both ultimately conclude 'External research does not establish the KnowledgeOS kernel.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Given the external evidence corpus, what is the smallest set of semantic and mechanical primitives that must be universally trustworthy for an organizational knowledge system — and which of those primitives are actually demonstrated as cross-cutting concerns in EKS, PKS, and AIP? ... let EKS/PKS/AIP evidence eliminate candidates, not merely confirm the research.
b_rows_sample.statement: Final commentary pass proposes the next precise research question (given the external evidence corpus, what is the smallest set of universally-trustworthy primitives, and which are demonstrated cross-cutting in EKS/PKS/AIP) plus a draft comparison matrix (Candidate x External evidence x EKS x PKS x AIP x Cross-cutting? x Kernel candidate?) for Identity, Provenance, Temporal validity, Authority, Evidence, Decision, Lineage, Lifecycle, Conflict, Assurance -- and states the crucial methodological principle that EKS/PKS/AIP evidence should be used to ELIMINATE candidates, not merely confirm the external research, 'to give a defensible KnowledgeOS kernel rather than a kernel designed from literature alone.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would not interpret DeepSeek's report as: 'We discovered the KnowledgeOS kernel.' b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit reframing/caution: DeepSeek's report should not be read as 'we discovered the KnowledgeOS kernel' but as 'EKS, PKS, and AIP already contain a recurring family of epistemic and governance invariants stronger than their current architectural boundaries suggest' -- a more valuable, more modest finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EKS invariant ↓ PKS equivalent ↓ AIP equivalent ↓ same semantic invariant? ↓ same lifecycle? ↓ same ownership? ↓ independent of domain? ↓ reusable abstraction? ↓ KERNEL CANDIDATE ↓ DDD validation ↓ KERNEL DECISION. b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a next-step progression (an 'AMENDMENT-6 progression'): for each candidate, verify EKS invariant -> PKS equivalent -> AIP equivalent -> same semantic invariant? -> same lifecycle? -> same ownership? -> independent of domain? -> reusable abstraction? -> kernel candidate -> DDD validation -> kernel decision; explicitly states this progression has not yet been executed for any candidate, and recommends starting with C-1 (Authority-as-recorded-reference-to-a-human-act) as the strongest, since DeepSeek found essentially the same invariant explicitly represented across all three systems.

b_rows_sample.statement: LLM-comparison validation (5 candidates, validated not assumed): persistent epistemic identity -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (a stateless generative model cannot possess it by construction; scaffolding like RAG cannot grant identity, only look up stored identities); historical belief evolution -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (generation is stateless, no belief to evolve); provenance preservation, contradiction management, justification accountability -- each a DEGRADATION, not an absence (an LLM can be scaffolded to approximate each, weakly).
