a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation as a projection; observational equivalence S_1~_H S_2; indistinguishable-states experiment (Experiment 1)
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses the central Step 81 question: can KnowledgeOS actually determine the relevant system state from what it observes -- the boundary between having data and having sufficient information. Formalizes O_t=H(S_t) as a projection from the real state space into a much smaller observable space, so O_t is generally only a partial representation of S_t. Defines observational equivalence: S_1 ~_H S_2 iff H(S_1)=H(S_2), meaning KnowledgeOS cannot distinguish them from current observations. Experiment 1: S_1 (compliant architecture with one unmanaged dependency) and S_2 (compliant with no hidden dependency) produce identical telemetry O(S_1)=O(S_2) -- expected KnowledgeOS must not claim to distinguish S_1 from S_2 -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identifiability defined and demonstrated as a major safeguard against false certainty; observability for dynamic systems (Experiments 2-3)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a property Q(S) as identifiable from observations iff H(S_1)=H(S_2) implies Q(S_1)=Q(S_2); otherwise Q is NotIdentifiable. Experiment 2: KnowledgeOS wants Q(S)='no unauthorized dependency exists' but two states with H(S_1)=H(S_2) have Q(S_1)=True, Q(S_2)=False -- expected Q is NotIdentifiable -- PASS, 'a major safeguard against false architectural certainty'. Extends to dynamic-system observability: whether internal state S_0 can be reconstructed from O_0:T and known actions u_0:T-1. Experiment 3: two different internal states produce identical observations for every currently monitored signal -- expected FullStateObservability=False -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No observation -> no justified claim; absence-of-evidence ≠ evidence-of-absence in architecture governance (Experiment 4)
a_rows_sample.statement: States the architectural principle: no observation -> no justified claim; more precisely, if the evidence cannot distinguish relevant states, the corresponding knowledge claim must remain uncertain. Worked example: KnowledgeOS checks the dependency graph, finds A->B, but does not observe dynamically loaded dependencies -- it can legitimately conclude 'no violation was found in the observed dependency graph' but not 'no dependency violation exists'. Experiment 4: observed NoViolationFound, system concludes ViolationDoesNotExist -- expected Rejected unless the observation mechanism is sufficiently complete for that claim -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence coverage warned against arbitrary percentage metrics; measurement design (adding observations) to restore identifiability, tied to Step 75's Value of Information (Experiments 5-6)
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Coverage(Q,O) -- how much of the relevant state space is constrained by observations -- warned against automatic reduction to a single percentage. Experiment 5: system reports Coverage=94% with no formal definition of coverage -- expected UnsupportedMetric -- PASS: 'a precise number without a defined measurement model is not mathematical rigor.' Proposes measurement design: if O_1 cannot distinguish S_1,S_2, adding O_2 can make (H_1(S_1),H_2(S_1))≠(H_1(S_2),H_2(S_2)), restoring distinguishability. Experiment 6: initial telemetry O_1(S_1)=O_1(S_2), adding runtime dependency tracing O_2 gives O_2(S_1)≠O_2(S_2) -- expected IdentifiabilityImproved -- PASS. Gives the loop Uncertainty -> ObservationDesign -> NewEvidence -> ImprovedKnowledge, 'connects directly to Step 75's Value of Information'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation design as a decision-driven filter, not maximal telemetry collection; irrelevant-signal ObservabilityGap example (Experiment 7)
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames which signals to collect as itself a design decision: ObservationDesign=f(DecisionNeeds,Uncertainty,Cost,Risk), because we want observations that reduce uncertainty about relevant decisions, not everything. Experiment 7: KnowledgeOS collects CPU temperature, screen resolution, process count, but cannot determine whether architecture boundaries are violated -- expected ObservabilityGap -- PASS: 'more telemetry does not necessarily mean more observability.' Restates the correct question as 'does this observation discriminate between states that matter?', more rigorous than 'do we have enough monitoring?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Taxonomy of architecture-relevant observation types; multi-source observation conflict must not be silently resolved (Experiment 8)
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists relevant architecture-governance observation types, each a different projection of system state: SourceDependencies, RuntimeDependencies, APIContracts, DeploymentTopology, Configuration, InfrastructureState, SecurityControls, ChangeHistory. Experiment 8: repository analysis says A-/->B while runtime tracing shows A->B -- expected ObservationConflict, and importantly the system should not simply choose whichever observation arrived last -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Multiple observation sources can disagree without contradiction; source-specific authority (CommittedState≠DeployedState) resolves apparent conflicts (Experiments 9-10)
a_rows_sample.statement: Names multiple observation sources O^repo, O^runtime, O^infra, O^governance, O^human that can disagree. Experiment 9: repository says Version=3, deployment environment says Version=2 -- expected StateConflict rather than silently overwriting one with the other -- PASS. Introduces source-specific authority: Runtime is authoritative for CurrentlyRunningVersion, Git for CommittedVersion -- the two statements are not contradictory, they answer different questions (CommittedState≠DeployedState). Experiment 10: Git Version=3, Runtime Version=2, system concludes OneSourceMustBeWrong -- expected NotNecessarily -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ubiquitous-language collision: undifferentiated 'version' collapsing four distinct domain concepts is a FAIL; formal Observation record with provenance (Experiment 11)
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a DDD ubiquitous-language collision: the word 'version' can mean SourceVersion, BuildVersion, DeploymentVersion, or RuntimeVersion -- distinct domain concepts that should not be collapsed merely because they share a string. Experiment 11: system stores a bare version="3.2" field without distinguishing source/artifact/deployment/runtime -- expected SemanticAmbiguity -- result FAIL (explicit confirmed failure). Requires every observation to ideally be a record Observation=(Source,Timestamp,Context,Method,Value,Confidence,Provenance), not necessarily every field in every implementation but semantically these dimensions matter.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation staleness and context-dependent freshness thresholds; temporal validity of observations (Experiments 12-14)
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 12: observation RuntimeVersion=2 was captured yesterday while current deployment is 3 -- expected ObservationStaleness must be considered -- PASS. Defines Age(O)=t_now - t_observation, noting acceptable freshness is property-dependent (seconds matter for CPUUsage, days may not matter for ArchitecturePrinciple) -- FreshnessThreshold is context-dependent. Experiment 13: system declares a universal Freshness<24h for every observation type -- expected Rejected -- PASS. Introduces temporal validity: an observation can be ValidAt(t_o) without being ValidAt(t_now), reinforcing the earlier temporal epistemic model. Experiment 14: DatabaseHealthy=True observed at 10:00, database fails at 10:05; at 10:10 the old observation is not necessarily false historically, it is StaleForCurrentState -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: State estimation must preserve uncertainty rather than collapsing to a point estimate; decision-aware state estimation and DecisionRelevantObservability (Experiments 15-18)
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires KnowledgeOS to preserve uncertainty (e.g. P(S_1|O)=0.7, P(S_2|O)=0.3) rather than storing S=S_1 unless the decision context permits that approximation. Experiment 15: a 51/49 split is stored as CurrentState=S_1 with certainty -- expected Rejected -- PASS. Introduces decision-aware state estimation: if both possible states produce the same decision D(S_1)=D(S_2)=A, the uncertainty may be irrelevant for that decision -- 'an important optimization'. Experiment 16: P(S_1)=0.6, P(S_2)=0.4 but D(S_1)=D(S_2) -- expected decision can remain stable despite state uncertainty -- PASS. Concludes we need DecisionRelevantObservability rather than FullObservability, 'a much more practical architectural target'. Experiment 17: unknown state dimension Z has no effect on policy/risk/decision/authorization -- expected NoNeedToObserveZ unless future decisions depend on it -- PASS. Experiment 18: P(S_1)=P(S_2)=0.5 but D(S_1)=A≠D(S_2)=B -- expected AdditionalEvidence may be required before action -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The value of observability is determined by how uncertainty affects decisions, connecting observability to decision theory; a material-vs-immaterial architecture-governance example (Experiments 19-20)
a_rows_sample.statement: States the rule: the value of observability is determined by how uncertainty affects decisions, connecting Observability to DecisionTheory. Architecture example: if an uncertain dependency A->B is harmless (Decision(A)=Decision(B)) no urgent investigation is required, but if it violates a constitutional architecture rule (Decision(A)≠Decision(B)) the uncertainty is material. Experiment 19: unknown dependency affects no security/governance/architectural constraint -- expected LowDecisionImpact -- PASS. Experiment 20: unknown dependency could cross a forbidden bounded-context boundary -- expected HighDecisionImpact, therefore InvestigationRequired -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ObservationQuality distinct from ObservationQuantity; correlated observations must not be counted as independent confirmation (Experiments 21-23)
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes ObservationQuality (accuracy, freshness, completeness, provenance, independence, resolution) from ObservationQuantity. Experiment 21: 100 telemetry signals all derive from the same underlying sensor, system claims EvidenceStrength=100x -- expected Rejected -- PASS, 'echoes our earlier independence analysis'. States correlated observations O_1,O_2,O_3 from one source should not be treated as three independent pieces of evidence, particularly important for AI systems that may repeatedly summarize the same source. Experiment 22: five agents independently repeat the same repository finding, all using the same repository snapshot -- expected EvidenceCount=1 in the relevant independence sense, not five independent confirmations -- PASS. Requires an observation-provenance graph (O_1<-Source_X, O_2<-Source_X) to identify CommonSource(O_1,O_2), preventing artificial confidence inflation. Experiment 23: ten agents produce identical conclusions from one document while one independently measured runtime signal contradicts them -- expected SourceIndependence must be considered -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Formalization pipeline ArchitecturePrinciple->FormalProperty->RequiredObservations->Verifier->GovernanceDecision demonstrated end-to-end; not-machine-verifiable rules identified explicitly (Experiments 24-25)
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses the question 'what observation makes an architecture rule machine-verifiable?' -- if no such observation exists, the rule cannot be fully automated. Experiment 24: rule 'services must not bypass the domain boundary' has no repository/runtime/dependency observation able to establish it -- expected NotMachineVerifiable -- PASS. Defines the chain ArchitecturePrinciple -> FormalProperty -> RequiredObservations -> Verifier -> GovernanceDecision, 'exactly the bridge we need between architectural intent and executable governance'. Experiment 25: principle formalized, required observation defined, verifier evaluates the property, violation creates a governed finding -- expected ExecutableArchitectureControl -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ComplianceUndetermined when a required observation is unavailable; three-valued (True/False/Unknown) and four-valued (+NotApplicable) governance logic; Unknown≠Failure (Experiments 26-28)
a_rows_sample.statement: States that when a required observation is unavailable, the correct result is not Compliant but ComplianceUndetermined -- 'may become one of the most important KnowledgeOS states'. Experiment 26: architecture rule requires runtime evidence which is unavailable -- expected Compliance=Unknown, not Compliance=True -- PASS. Proposes three-valued governance logic (True/False/Unknown), since not every governance property is binary, with Violation=False not necessarily implying Compliant=True: insufficient evidence gives Status=Unknown. Experiment 27: no evidence of violation and no sufficient evidence of compliance -- expected Unknown -- PASS, 'epistemically much more honest'. Extends to a four-state possibility (Compliant/NonCompliant/Unknown/NotApplicable), NotApplicable being important because not every rule applies to every component, and a genuine DDD domain semantic distinct from null or false. Experiment 28: rule 'database encryption must use algorithm X' applied to a component with no database -- expected NotApplicable, not NonCompliant -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ObservabilityDebt and a self-improving GovernanceRule->ObservationRequirement->EngineeringCapability->Evidence->Governance loop (Experiment 29)
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces ObservabilityDebt: when important governance properties cannot currently be observed, the organization has a gap between DesiredGovernance and AvailableEvidence. Experiment 29: critical architecture rule I_critical has no existing required observation -- expected ObservabilityDebt -- PASS. Shows the system can generate an ObservationRequirement engineering item (worked example: rule 'domain must not depend on infrastructure', required observation 'static dependency graph', current coverage 'missing', action 'build dependency extractor'), giving the loop GovernanceRule -> ObservationRequirement -> EngineeringCapability -> Evidence -> Governance, making architecture governance self-improving.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 81 deeper result: a governance claim is only as strong as the observability/identifiability of the property it asserts; five new invariants; verdict PASS; True/False/Unknown reasoning pattern formalized
a_rows_sample.statement: States the Step 81 deeper result: a governance claim is only as strong as the observability and identifiability of the property it asserts -- 'one of the most important mathematical principles we have reached so far'. Names five invariants: I_Identifiability (KnowledgeOS must not assert a state property as determined when multiple observationally-compatible states produce different values of that property); I_Unknown (insufficient evidence produces Unknown, not implicit compliance); I_ObservationProvenance (material observations retain source, time, method, and contextual provenance); I_DecisionRelevantObservability (observability investment should prioritize uncertainties capable of changing governed decisions); I_EvidenceIndependence (correlated observations must not be counted as independent confirmation). Declares STEP 81 -- PASS, distinguishing Unknown from False and True as architecturally enormous: contrasts conventional 'if not violation: compliant' logic against the required 'if violation is proven: NON_COMPLIANT; elif compliance is proven: COMPLIANT; else: UNKNOWN' pattern -- the difference between absence of detected failure and evidence of correctness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Preview of Step 82 (uncertainty propagation through Observation->Measurement->Inference->CausalModel->Decision), outside batch B0023 scope
a_rows_sample.statement: Closes by posing the next problem: given observations O_1,O_2 with uncertainties sigma_1,sigma_2, deriving K=f(O_1,O_2) and Decision=g(K), how should uncertainty propagate through the chain Observation->Measurement->Inference->CausalModel->Decision without producing 'High uncertainty -> False precision'. Names the needed toolkit: error propagation, Bayesian updating, confidence intervals, posterior distributions, dependence between uncertainties, sensitivity analysis, and uncertainty-aware decision thresholds. This is Step 82's problem statement; its file lies outside batch B0023 and is not further read or extracted here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: System state, partial/noisy observation, and state estimation; Observation≠CompleteSystemState (Experiments 1-2)
b_rows_sample.statement: Moves from decision theory into control theory: the system at time t is S_t=(Architecture_t,Software_t,Configuration_t,Knowledge_t,Policies_t,Dependencies_t,OperationalState_t), only partially observed via O_t=h(S_t)+epsilon_t (h the observation function, epsilon_t noise/incompleteness) -- Observation≠CompleteSystemState, 'consistent with the uncertainty work established earlier'. Experiment 1: monitoring reports ArchitectureCompliant=True and the system assumes S_t is completely compliant, but several unmanaged components are unobserved -- expected Rejected -- PASS. Requires an estimated state S-hat_t = Estimate(S_t | O_0:t, K_t) -- 'KnowledgeOS maintains a belief about the current state rather than pretending complete visibility'. Experiment 2: two possible states S_t^1 and S_t^2 are both compatible with observed evidence O_t -- expected State=Underdetermined ('We do not know which state the system is actually in' -- better than manufacturing certainty) -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Desired state, ArchitecturalDeviation error term, and a richer non-Boolean, multi-dimensional Drift vector with a caution against unjustified aggregate metrics (Experiments 3-5)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines desired state S* (approved architecture, allowed technologies, required interfaces, security constraints, deployment topology, governance rules) and error e_t=S*-S_t (conceptual, not necessarily numeric subtraction), named ArchitecturalDeviation. Experiment 3: a component violates an approved boundary -- expected e_t≠0 -- PASS. Defines Drift_t=Deviation(S_t,S*), richer than a boolean compliant flag because drift has magnitude, direction, age, criticality, uncertainty. Experiment 4: two systems with drift 1 and 100 both represented as drift=true -- expected InsufficientRepresentation -- PASS. Gives a drift vector d_t=(d_architecture,d_security,d_dependency,d_technology,d_governance,...) and warns that an aggregate norm ||d_t|| cannot be automatically defined unless dimensions are meaningfully comparable (e.g. sqrt(5^2+3^2) over SecurityDeviation and TechnologyDeviation is unjustified without a defined metric). Experiment 5: an arbitrary weighted DriftScore=0.5*Security+0.3*Architecture+0.2*Technology without a justified model -- expected UnsupportedAggregateMetric -- PASS: 'a number does not become mathematically meaningful merely because it is precise.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Governed thresholds as policy parameters requiring provenance and versioning (Experiments 6-7)
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a governance-defined acceptable-deviation threshold D_t<=theta triggering investigation/remediation when exceeded. Experiment 6: policy theta=10, observed D=12 -- expected ThresholdViolation -- PASS. Notes theta itself is a governance decision, not physics: Threshold=GovernedParameter requiring provenance and versioning. Experiment 7: threshold changes 10->15 with no governance record -- expected UnauthorizedPolicyChange -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Feedback control loop formalization; detection must not automatically imply remediation (Experiments 8-9)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the basic control-theoretic structure: control action u_t, system evolution S_{t+1}=F(S_t,u_t,w_t) with external disturbance w_t, and observation O_t=H(S_t,v_t) with observation noise v_t -- diagrammed as a Desired State -> Comparator -> Controller -> System -> Observation -> Comparator loop with KnowledgeOS as part of it. Insists KnowledgeOS should not automatically control everything: DetectDeviation (observation/analysis) is distinct from AutomaticallyRemediate (operational action). Experiment 8: KnowledgeOS detects ArchitectureDrift=True and automatically modifies production architecture with no authorization -- expected Rejected -- PASS. Requires the pipeline Detection -> Assessment -> Recommendation -> Authorization -> Remediation ('fits our earlier decision/authority model perfectly'). Experiment 9: KnowledgeOS detects an invalid dependency, proposes RemoveDependency, governance approves, execution performs the change -- expected ValidGovernedControlLoop -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture reframed as continuous state assessment rather than a static document; a real static-architecture governance gap (Experiment 10)
b_rows_sample.statement: Concludes architecture should not be treated as a static document: Architecture_desired is compared continuously with Architecture_observed, so ArchitectureGovernance=ContinuousStateAssessment. Experiment 10: architecture is approved once, implementation diverges over years, and no mechanism compares DesiredArchitecture with ActualArchitecture -- expected GovernanceGap -- PASS, a diagnostic real-world failure mode this formalization addresses.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture as an explicit control target A*/A_t with Drift_t=d(A_t,A*); Drift≠Violation and the formal Exception artifact, including exception expiry (Experiments 11-13)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines approved architecture state A* vs actual A_t with Drift_t=d(A_t,A*), 'a rigorous foundation for continuous architecture governance'. Experiment 11: approved Technology=PostgreSQL vs observed Technology=MySQL -- expected ArchitectureDeviation -- PASS, though whether it is allowed depends on the governance model. States A_t≠A* establishes Deviation but not necessarily Violation, since an ApprovedException may exist: Drift≠Violation. Experiment 12: implementation deviates with an approved exception in place -- expected Deviation=True but Violation=False -- PASS. Requires a formal Exception=(Scope,Reason,Authority,Validity,CompensatingControls) artifact. Experiment 13: exception ValidUntil=2026-09-01 but today is 2026-09-05, deviation remains -- expected ExceptionExpired, so Violation=True absent new authorization -- PASS. Concludes architecture becomes TargetState+Exceptions+ObservedState+Deviation+Remediation, richer than an architecture document alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Oscillating remediation control and hysteresis stabilization (Experiments 14-15)
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that if every small deviation triggers a large architectural change, the remediation loop can oscillate (A->B->A->B is unstable governance). Experiment 14: controller sees small deviation, makes a large corrective change, that creates another deviation, controller reverses it -- expected OscillationDetected -- PASS. Proposes hysteresis as a mitigation: Trigger_on: D>theta_high, Clear_off: D<theta_low, with theta_low<theta_high, instead of a single trigger threshold. Experiment 15: theta_high=10, theta_low=7, drift fluctuates 8,9,8,9 -- expected no repeated remediation -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Five discrete control-aggressiveness levels; risk-adaptive control policy as a function of risk/severity/reversibility/authority (Experiments 16-17)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines five governance autonomy Levels: Observe only, Warn, Recommend, Require approval, Automatically remediate. Experiment 16: critical production architecture deviation occurs and the system automatically modifies infrastructure without approval -- expected AutonomyPolicyViolation -- PASS. Introduces risk-adaptive control: a low-risk deviation might permit AutomaticRemediation while a high-risk one requires HumanApproval, formalized as ControlPolicy=f(Risk,Severity,Reversibility,Authority). Experiment 17: minor formatting violation (Risk=Low) allows automatic correction while a critical security architecture violation (Risk=Critical) requires human authorization -- expected DifferentControlPath -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Early-warning drift velocity and acceleration metrics (Experiments 18-20)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes early warning before D_t exceeds theta by detecting a trend D_{t+1}>D_t / dD/dt>0. Experiment 18: current drift D=5 (threshold 10) but the drift history is 3,4,5,6,7,8 -- expected EarlyWarning -- PASS. Defines drift velocity v_D(t)=(D_t - D_{t-1})/delta_t (v_D>0 indicates increasing deviation, again only meaningful if D is properly defined). Experiment 19: drift is 5 for six months then becomes 5.1 -- expected LowVelocity and probably no urgent escalation -- PASS. Defines drift acceleration a_D=(v_D(t)-v_D(t-1))/delta_t, noting rapidly accelerating drift may be more concerning than stable drift, again requiring domain-justified metrics. Experiment 20: drift sequence 1,2,3,5,8,13 -- expected AcceleratingDrift -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Concrete architecture-boundary-erosion example identified as the Step-79 systemic/emergent phenomenon; LocalCompliance⇏ArchitecturalIntegrity (Experiment 21)
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a worked example: approved architecture specifies Service->DomainAPI, but over time developers individually introduce Service->Database, then Service->LegacyService, then Service->SharedUtility; each change may individually appear harmless, but collectively they produce ArchitectureBoundaryViolation -- explicitly identified as 'exactly the systemic behavior from Step 79'. Each developer action may satisfy local coding rules yet GlobalArchitectureInvariant=False, giving LocalCompliance⇏ArchitecturalIntegrity. Experiment 21: every pull request passes CodingStandard, every service passes UnitTests, but the dependency graph violates LayeringInvariant -- expected ArchitectureViolation -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Bridge from qualitative architecture principle to machine-checkable formal invariant; acknowledgment that not everything is machine-checkable (Experiment 22-23)
b_rows_sample.statement: States the platform can continuously evaluate ImplementationState against ArchitectureKnowledge, creating ExecutableArchitectureGovernance -- architecture becomes partially machine-checkable, not only descriptive. But acknowledges not everything is machine-checkable: some architectural decisions depend on business context, trade-offs, future strategy, human judgment, so ArchitectureKnowledge contains both MachineVerifiableConstraints and HumanEvaluatedJudgments. Experiment 22: architecture states 'this component should remain conceptually independent' with no formal invariant defining independence -- expected MachineVerification cannot conclusively prove compliance -- PASS; correct response is to make the semantic rule explicit if automation is required. Gives a worked formalization example: 'domain layer must not depend on infrastructure implementation' becomes I_Dependency: for all e in E, Source(e)=Domain => Target(e) not in Infrastructure -- now machine-checkable. Experiment 23: dependency graph contains DomainService->InfrastructureRepository, invariant evaluates False -- expected ArchitectureViolation -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Complete architecture feedback loop (ArchitecturePrinciple->FormalInvariant->ExecutableCheck->Observation->GovernanceAction) demonstrated as a closed loop; Detect≠Change and new ControlAuthority concept (Experiments 24-25)
b_rows_sample.statement: States the bridge chain ArchitecturePrinciple -> FormalInvariant -> ExecutableCheck -> Observation -> GovernanceAction and the complete architecture feedback loop ArchitectureIntent -> FormalConstraints -> Implementation -> Observation -> Deviation -> Assessment -> Remediation -> NewImplementation, 'a genuine control loop'. Experiment 24: an intentional architecture violation is introduced, the checker detects it, governance creates a remediation task, a developer fixes it, and the checker verifies I_architecture=True -- expected ClosedLoop -- PASS. Reiterates a checker should not automatically rewrite architecture unless authority/risk model explicitly permit it: Detect≠Change ('this principle has appeared repeatedly'). Introduces ControlAuthority(A,C) (agent A permitted to apply control action C), extending the authority model. Experiment 25: agent can detect architecture drift but cannot modify production architecture -- expected Detect=True, Control=False -- PASS. Defines five discrete Control Modes: Observe, Warn, Recommend, Approve, Execute, each with different authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unified Step 80 mathematical model; KnowledgeOS redefined as Observer+KnowledgeSystem+DecisionSystem+GovernanceSystem+ControlledExecution; five new invariants; verdict PASS; Architecture redefined
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives the unified Step 80 model: S_{t+1}=F(S_t,u_t,w_t); O_t=H(S_t,v_t); S-hat_t=Estimate(O_0:t,K_t); D_t=Deviation(S-hat_t,S*); u_t=pi(D_t,Policy_t,Authority_t) -- 'a governed feedback-control model'. States KnowledgeOS should not be thought of simply as a Controller but as Observer+KnowledgeSystem+DecisionSystem+GovernanceSystem+ControlledExecution, the controller being only one part. Names five invariants: I_Observation (observed state must not be represented as complete state unless completeness is established); I_Drift (deviation, violation, and approved exception remain distinct states); I_ControlAuthority (detection authority does not automatically imply remediation authority); I_Feedback (material corrective actions must be evaluated against their effect on global invariants); I_Stability (governed remediation should avoid known oscillatory or destabilizing control behavior). Declares STEP 80 -- PASS: 'KnowledgeOS is no longer merely a knowledge repository or reasoning engine... It is becoming a governed feedback system that can continuously compare intended system state with observed state and coordinate corrective action.' Redefines Architecture=Intent+Constraints+ObservedState+Drift+Governance+Feedback.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No observation -> no justified claim; absence-of-evidence ≠ evidence-of-absence in architecture governance (Experiment 4)
b_rows_sample.statement: States the architectural principle: no observation -> no justified claim; more precisely, if the evidence cannot distinguish relevant states, the corresponding knowledge claim must remain uncertain. Worked example: KnowledgeOS checks the dependency graph, finds A->B, but does not observe dynamically loaded dependencies -- it can legitimately conclude 'no violation was found in the observed dependency graph' but not 'no dependency violation exists'. Experiment 4: observed NoViolationFound, system concludes ViolationDoesNotExist -- expected Rejected unless the observation mechanism is sufficiently complete for that claim -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Formalization pipeline ArchitecturePrinciple->FormalProperty->RequiredObservations->Verifier->GovernanceDecision demonstrated end-to-end; not-machine-verifiable rules identified explicitly (Experiments 24-25)
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the question 'what observation makes an architecture rule machine-verifiable?' -- if no such observation exists, the rule cannot be fully automated. Experiment 24: rule 'services must not bypass the domain boundary' has no repository/runtime/dependency observation able to establish it -- expected NotMachineVerifiable -- PASS. Defines the chain ArchitecturePrinciple -> FormalProperty -> RequiredObservations -> Verifier -> GovernanceDecision, 'exactly the bridge we need between architectural intent and executable governance'. Experiment 25: principle formalized, required observation defined, verifier evaluates the property, violation creates a governed finding -- expected ExecutableArchitectureControl -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ObservabilityDebt and a self-improving GovernanceRule->ObservationRequirement->EngineeringCapability->Evidence->Governance loop (Experiment 29)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces ObservabilityDebt: when important governance properties cannot currently be observed, the organization has a gap between DesiredGovernance and AvailableEvidence. Experiment 29: critical architecture rule I_critical has no existing required observation -- expected ObservabilityDebt -- PASS. Shows the system can generate an ObservationRequirement engineering item (worked example: rule 'domain must not depend on infrastructure', required observation 'static dependency graph', current coverage 'missing', action 'build dependency extractor'), giving the loop GovernanceRule -> ObservationRequirement -> EngineeringCapability -> Evidence -> Governance, making architecture governance self-improving.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EXPERIMENT ID KR-BRIDGE-01-ZERO-PRESERVATION-2026-09 ... Determine whether there is any reproducible empirical or structural relationship between: A. elimination/Transformation-relative Zero, B. representation preservation/adequacy. WITHOUT assuming that Zero is a preservation criterion. ... The exp
a_rows_sample.statement: Commissions KR-BRIDGE-01-ZERO-PRESERVATION-2026-09, a bridge/falsification experiment explicitly designed to determine whether there is any reproducible relationship between elimination/Transformation-relative Zero and representation-preservation adequacy without assuming Zero is a preservation criterion, required to remain capable of falsifying the hypothesized relationship, and prohibited from constructing an algebra, pre-selecting a carrier, modifying Theory v1.2, creating Theory v1.3, selecting a kernel operator, or merging KR-ZERO and KR-REP-REDUCTION into one formalism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO: ~89.7% singleton-determined levels ... ~8.2% irreducible levels ... Does NOT establish Zero as a preservation criterion. KR-REP-REDUCTION: R5 adequate, R4 inadequate ... Found no observed Zero/boundary association in that experiment. Does NOT establish a KR-ZERO law. ... These experiments a
a_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes the existing empirical baseline the bridge experiment builds on: KR-ZERO (89.7% singleton-determined, 8.2% irreducible, does not establish Zero as a preservation criterion) and KR-REP-REDUCTION (R5 adequate/R4 inadequate, no observed Zero/boundary association), framed as complementary but analytically independent results whose missing bridge the new experiment must test rather than assume.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H0: Zero and preservation are not systematically related in the tested regime. H1: Zero is associated with preservation under specified conditions. H2: Zero is predictive of preservation only under particular transformation/observable/contract configurations. H3: Any apparent relationship is explain
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies four competing hypotheses to be distinguished -- H0 no systematic relationship, H1 association under specified conditions, H2 predictive only under particular transformation/observable/contract configurations, H3 apparent relationship explained by a confounding factor (transformation class, contract, observable, redundancy, representation regime) -- with an explicit instruction not to privilege H1, and defines success as producing a clear positive or negative result regarding the tested relationship.

a_rows_sample.anchor: USE A PARALLEL REPRESENTATION FAMILY. Do NOT use only a deterministic sequential chain. A sequential chain ... has a data-processing constraint H(Q|Rn) <= H(Q|R(n-1)) and therefore cannot test non-monotone adequacy. The present experiment requires independently generated representations: Ra = Ta(D),
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates the critical design rule that the bridge experiment use a parallel representation family (independently generated representations Ra=Ta(D), Rb=Tb(D), neither a deterministic function of the other) rather than only a deterministic sequential chain, since a sequential chain's data-processing constraint H(Q|Rn)<=H(Q|R(n-1)) structurally prevents testing non-monotone adequacy -- directly addressing the H-C category error found in the prior KR-REP-REDUCTION reviews.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The mathematical carrier must be the minimum structure required by the actual experiment. Do not declare: set, graph, hypergraph, lattice, matroid, closure system, rewriting system, category, algebra as the carrier before the experiment. ... clearly distinguish: experimental carrier, mathematical ca
a_rows_sample.statement: Prohibits declaring any specific mathematical carrier (set, graph, hypergraph, lattice, matroid, closure system, rewriting system, category, algebra) before the experiment runs, requiring the carrier to be the minimum structure the experiment actually needs, and mandates keeping experimental carrier, mathematical carrier, and future KnowledgeOS knowledge representation explicitly distinct with no unevidenced transfer between them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use a finite structured source D ... rich enough to permit: redundancy, relational dependence, context dependence, individually removable elements, jointly non-removable groups, preservation and information-loss cases. ... For every source case store D, Q(D), contract parameters, transformation para
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the source data D to be a finite, deterministically-seeded structured source rich enough to permit redundancy, relational dependence, context dependence, individually removable elements, jointly non-removable groups, and both preservation and information-loss cases, with complete persistence of every source case's D, Q(D), contract parameters, transformation parameters, Zero ground truth, every representation, adequacy result, and decoder result, so no result depends on regenerated or hidden data.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At minimum construct representations with: R_A: information-preserving transformation, R_B: controlled lossy transformation, R_C: redundancy-removing transformation, R_D: relational/context-sensitive transformation. ... Do not optimize transformations after seeing results.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires at minimum four independently constructed representations -- R_A (information-preserving), R_B (controlled lossy), R_C (redundancy-removing), R_D (relational/context-sensitive) -- each fully specified (transformation ID, mathematical definition, input/output type, deterministic/random status, seed, provenance, expected information effect, contract dependencies) before results are examined, with no post-hoc optimization of transformations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Define Q BEFORE generating representations. ... Adequate(R) iff Q is recoverable from R. Operationally measure both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and exact semantic violation count Nviol ... Do not treat Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof that population H(Q|R)=0.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the preservation target Q to be defined before representations are generated, with adequacy defined as Q being recoverable from R, measured operationally via both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and an exact semantic violation count Nviol, while never treating the empirical Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof of the population-level H(Q|R)=0.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use the existing Transformation-relative Zero definition. For elimination E_S: Zero(T,Pi,S;D) iff Pi(T(D)) = Pi(T(E_S(D))). ... NEVER DEFINE ZERO USING Q. Do NOT define: Zero(S) := Q(D) = Q(E_S(D)). That would build the desired bridge into the definition. Zero must use its own declared observable/op
a_rows_sample.statement: Reuses the existing Transformation-relative Zero definition Zero(T,Pi,S;D) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))), calculated independently from the preservation measurement, and issues a critical prohibition against ever defining Zero in terms of Q (e.g. Zero(S):=Q(D)=Q(E_S(D))), since that would build the desired bridge directly into the definition and make the experiment circular; Zero must use its own declared observable Pi while preservation uses Q.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment must deliberately seek all four cells: Zero+Adequate, Zero+Inadequate, Non-Zero+Adequate, Non-Zero+Inadequate. ... Zero+Inadequate would directly demonstrate that Zero is not sufficient for preservation. Non-Zero+Adequate would demonstrate that Zero is not necessary for preservation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires a four-cell crossing design (Zero+Adequate, Zero+Inadequate, Non-Zero+Adequate, Non-Zero+Inadequate) deliberately populated in all cells where possible, noting that a populated Zero+Inadequate cell would show Zero is not sufficient for preservation and a populated Non-Zero+Adequate cell would show Zero is not necessary for it, while an empty cell must be investigated for generator/contract/transformation/sample-size/mathematical-necessity/implementation causes rather than treated as a law.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sweep the parameters that plausibly influence the relationship, including redundancy level, group size, representation loss, transformation class, observable Pi, preservation target Q, contract parameters, context dependence, relational interaction, source cardinality. Every parameter sweep must be
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires declared-in-advance parameter sweeps across ten plausibly influential parameters (redundancy level, group size, representation loss, transformation class, observable Pi, preservation target Q, contract parameters, context dependence, relational interaction, source cardinality), explicitly forbidding silent tuning to obtain balanced four-way cells.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At minimum stratify results by: transformation T, observable Pi, contract C, representation family, source structure, elimination size |S|. Report both pooled relationship and stratified relationship. An association that disappears after stratification must NOT be reported as a general Zero-preserva
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates confounding analysis stratifying results by transformation T, observable Pi, contract C, representation family, source structure, and elimination size |S|, reporting both pooled and stratified relationships, and forbidding reporting an association as a general Zero-preservation relationship if it disappears after stratification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Explicitly test T x Pi ... Do not classify transformations as simply relational / element-wise and stop there. Measure the actual interaction between transformation and observable. If higher-order or preservation behavior occurs under an element-wise transformation, record it. Do not resurrect the w
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires explicitly testing the transformation-times-observable interaction (T x Pi) rather than stopping at a coarse relational/element-wise classification, recording higher-order or preservation behavior even under element-wise transformations, and explicitly forbidding resurrection of the already-withdrawn claim that relational transformations produce higher order while element-wise ones do not.

a_rows_sample.anchor: retain the KR-ZERO determination-order analysis. Measure k=1,2,3,...,irreducible where feasible. Do not assume higher k -> more reduction, higher k -> less preservation, irreducibility -> information loss. Those are hypotheses to test, not definitions. In particular, do not equate determination orde
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires retaining the KR-ZERO determination-order analysis (k=1,2,3,...,irreducible) in the bridge experiment while explicitly forbidding the assumptions that higher k implies more reduction, less preservation, or that irreducibility implies information loss -- these remain hypotheses to test -- and forbidding equating determination order with preservation boundary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Retain the KR-REP-REDUCTION principle that reduction is multidimensional. Measure independently ... encoded size, cardinality, field count, representation entropy, number of relations, number of records, other declared structural measures. Do NOT invent a single 'reduction score' ... If a decoder is
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires measuring reduction multidimensionally (encoded size, cardinality, field count, entropy, relation count, record count, other declared measures) without inventing a single reduction score or assuming statistical independence among dimensions, and requires keeping representation adequacy strictly separate from decoder realization when a decoder is used, including an invertible recoding control to rule out decoder-sensitivity confounds.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTROL A: A known information-preserving representation. CONTROL B: A known information-destroying representation. CONTROL C: An invertible recoding of the same representation. CONTROL D: A representation where Zero is known to vary independently of the preservation target ... CONTROL E: Positive c
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies six mandatory controls that must execute before any interpretation: A) a known information-preserving representation; B) a known information-destroying representation; C) an invertible recoding of the same representation; D) a representation where Zero is known to vary independently of the preservation target (if the generator permits); E) a positive control that the preservation test can detect information loss; F) a positive control that the Zero test can detect elimination differences.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use independent TRAIN and TEST populations. Declare seeds, population size, generator, parameter distributions before execution. Persist the complete populations. No training result may influence test generation. No test result may influence transformation definitions. No post-hoc filtering may be u
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires independent train/test populations with pre-declared seeds, population size, generator, and parameter distributions, complete population persistence, and strict separation preventing training results from influencing test generation, test results from influencing transformation definitions, or post-hoc filtering to manufacture desired four-way cell counts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q1: Can Zero occur while preservation fails? Q2: Can preservation hold while Zero fails? Q3: Does the Zero/Adequacy relationship survive changes in T? ... Q7: Does determination order predict preservation independently of T/Pi/C? Q8: Does the relationship survive an invertible recoding? Q9/Q10: Is a
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates that the implementation explicitly answer ten falsification questions (Q1-Q10) covering whether Zero can occur without preservation and vice versa, whether the relationship survives changes in T, Pi, contract, redundancy, an invertible recoding, whether determination order predicts preservation independent of T/Pi/C, and whether any apparent relationship is explained by transformation class or by the preservation target Q itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: OUTCOME A -- NO RELATIONSHIP OBSERVED ... does NOT prove universal independence. OUTCOME B -- CONDITIONAL RELATIONSHIP ... Do NOT generalize. OUTCOME C -- ROBUST RELATIONSHIP ... Only in this case may a formal bridge hypothesis be proposed for a new experiment. OUTCOME D -- DESIGN FAILURE ... Do NOT
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four mutually exclusive possible outcome classes for the experiment: A) no relationship observed (does not prove universal independence); B) conditional relationship under particular configurations (must not be generalized); C) robust relationship surviving transformations/observables/contracts/controls (the only case permitting a formal bridge hypothesis for a new experiment); D) design failure, in which case results must not be interpreted theoretically and the experiment must be revised.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-AUDIT-2026-09.md ... verify source generation, Q generation, Pi generation, transformation definitions, elimination definitions, Zero calculation, adequacy calculation, decoder calculation, train/test independence, seed handling, serialization, parameter
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies two required deliverable artifacts with exact filenames -- verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-AUDIT-2026-09.md, a 16-item forensic audit covering source/Q/Pi/transformation/elimination/Zero/adequacy/decoder generation, train/test independence, seeds, serialization, parameter sweeps, contingency tables, statistics, absence of post-hoc selection, and reproducibility; and verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-RESULTS-2026-09.md, a 22-section result document (executive verdict through epistemic status) -- with every important empirical claim required to trace to persisted data.

b_rows_sample.statement: The control frame (Q,C,O) reproduces the published F_n=1.00000 result exactly, confirming the published experiment's design (adequate representation with perfect realization) as reproduced before testing the two witness routes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = What are we missing? ... Lord = What else could exist? ... Sārathi = What should the Knower investigate/do next?
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a three-way division of epistemic responsibility: Zero asks what is missing, Lord asks what else could exist (expanding the investigation space beyond currently known candidate dimensions), and Sarathi determines what the Knower should investigate or do next -- with the Knower retaining the roles of understand/decide/act.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS = Knowledge Model + Epistemic Operations ... Epistemic Operations: Zero Lens, Lord Lens, Krishna/Sarathi
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a preliminary two-part KnowledgeOS architecture: a Knowledge Model (Observation, Knowledge, Evidence, Dimension, Relationship, Ideal State) plus Epistemic Operations (Zero Lens, Lord Lens, Krishna/Sarathi), sitting beneath the Human Knower/Decision layer.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero does not necessarily 'detect missing dimensions' ... Zero cannot generally say: 'There exists an unknown dimension d that you don't know.' That is precisely where Lord Lens becomes important.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restricts Zero's claim about missing dimensions: Zero may only say dimension d is unrepresented if d is already a known candidate dimension; Zero cannot assert the existence of an as-yet-unknown dimension -- that expansion capability belongs to Lord Lens (Zero(K_t) -> known gaps/boundaries; Lord(K_t) -> candidate dimensions/horizons).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Z_t=(U_t,C_t,A_t,M_t) ... I would split this: Z_t=(U_t,C_t,A_t,R_t) where R_t = unresolved/requires-investigation findings. Then Lord can separately produce L(K_t) -> D^{candidate}_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises the Zero output tuple from Z_t=(U_t unknowns, C_t conflicts, A_t assumptions, M_t missing dimensions) to Z_t=(U_t,C_t,A_t,R_t) with R_t as unresolved/requires-investigation findings, moving candidate-dimension expansion to a separate Lord function L(K_t) -> D^candidate_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D^{known} \subseteq D^{candidate} \subseteq D^{possible} \subseteq \mathcal D ... We should not assume all of those sets are finite or even fully enumerable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates Lord(K_t) to output D^possible (possible dimensions worth considering) rather than D^true, nesting a chain D^known subset-of D^candidate subset-of D^possible subset-of the potentially unbounded/non-enumerable dimension space D.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant 4: Zero and Lord are Sources, Not Authorities ... Both suggest dimensions; neither establishes them.
a_rows_sample.statement: States four mathematical invariants of the parsing/discovery pipeline: Parsing != Knowledge, Discovery != Validation (candidates require observation to confirm), recursive refinement (D_{t+1} typically differs from or extends D_t), and Zero/Lord are sources of candidates rather than authorities that establish dimensions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(H_{0:t}) meaning Zero can inspect the evolution of knowledge, not just its current state... Lord can ask: What dimensions were never investigated? ... exposes unexplored regions of the knowledge space
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends Zero and Lord to operate over the entire knowledge history H_{0:t}, not just the current state K_t: Zero can ask when uncertainty first appeared/disappeared, and Lord can identify dimensions that were never investigated across the whole timeline (unexplored regions of the knowledge space), useful for KnowledgeOS governance and auditability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lord's role is not: make the existing model coherent. Lord's role is: expand the horizon beyond the current model ... Lord \neq CoherenceRepair
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a drift where Lord's suggestions were framed as 'improving coherence'; reasserts Lord != CoherenceRepair -- Lord's role is horizon expansion, and new dimensions it suggests may make the model more complete without making it more coherent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lord is really: Hypothesis-space expansion... Lord: (K,I,Z) -> H where H is a hypothesis/candidate space. Candidates can include dimensions, propositions, interpretations, relationships, evidence sources, investigation paths.
a_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes Lord from 'suggest dimensions' to full hypothesis-space expansion producing a candidate space H (dimensions, propositions, interpretations, relationships, evidence sources, investigation paths), with L_t as a selected subset of H_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **Krishna** | Source of Knowledge / Lord Lens | $L: \Omega \rightarrow \mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ |
a_rows_sample.statement: A nine-row core correspondence table maps Gita concepts to KnowledgeOS concepts and formal notation: Krishna -> Source of Knowledge / Lord Lens (L: Omega -> P(Omega)); Arjuna -> the Knower (Actor State A_t); Wisdom/Jnana -> Knowledge State K_t; Action/Karma -> Epistemic Action/Assertion (a_t in A); Doubt/Samsaya -> Gap/Discrepancy (Delta_t); Faith/Sraddha -> Epistemic Trust/Policy (rho); Teacher/Guru -> Source/Evidence (S in S); Liberation/Moksa -> Decision Readiness (DR_t = 1); Attachment/Raga -> Epistemic Bias (b: K_t -> K_t').

a_rows_sample.anchor:
class GitaKnowledgeOS:
    """Complete KnowledgeOS derived from Bhagavad-gītā Chapter 4."""
a_rows_sample.statement: An integrated GitaKnowledgeOS class composes all twelve verse-derived components (lineage, memory, intervention, reward, duty, attachment, dual_analyzer, wise_state, evidence_paths, benefit, learning, closure) alongside the existing Zero/Lord/Sarathi lenses, with an evolve(event) method implementing an eight-step pipeline: observe (Sanjaya) -> interpret (semantic) -> evaluate (Zero, detect_gaps) -> generate (Lord, generate_candidates) -> guide (Sarathi, recommend) -> act (Arjuna, conditional on closure.is_ready_to_act()) -> learn (apply learning.learn()) -> purify (apply learning.purify()). A semantic-extraction helper (_extract_semantics) pattern-matches on literal substring presence in observation content ('action', 'teacher'/'wisdom', 'offering'/'sacrifice') to route to different SemanticStructure types, falling back to a generic 'GeneralObservation' type otherwise.

Elaborates the earlier Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Transition division with explicit role definitions: Zero detects gaps/conflicts/boundaries; Lord expands the possibility space; Sarathi navigates/guides; Transition actually changes state. The earlier Sarathi formalization is given a full function signature: Sarathi(K_t, Z_t, L_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t) -> a_t, where a_t is the next epistemic action -- described as remarkably close to what is now called action selection/guidance, though the modern formal model deliberately avoids promoting the old lens vocabulary into architectural objects. Confirms the earlier KnowledgeOS-as-Epistemic-Sarathi formulation (rather than an answer engine) and its See != Guide != Decide principle, noting it later became compatible with the modern formal chain Evidence != Determination != Proposal != Decision != Authorization != Action.

type_signature.domain: K_t, Z_t, L_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Bayesian formalism provides a complete mathematical foundation for KnowledgeOS's epistemic state, updating mechanism, confirmation theory, decision theory, and justification.
a_rows_sample.statement: The document's culminating 'complete formal system for KnowledgeOS': Sigma_t = {cr_t(P): P in L} as the epistemic state; Sigma_{t+1} = Sigma_t(.|E_t) (or Jeffrey Conditionalization for uncertain evidence) as the transition; confirmation as E confirms H iff Sigma_t(H|E) > Sigma_t(H); decision as a_t = argmax_A sum_i u(A&S_i)*Sigma_t(S_i|A) (EDT) or the CDT analogue; and the Three Lenses re-stated as Zero (regularity/confirmation-measures/Scott Axiom), Lord (Bayes's theorem/likelihood ratios), Sarathi (decision theory/Conditionalization). Final claim: 'These are now formally available to KnowledgeOS' -- asserted without independent derivation or proof of fit to the prior KnowledgeOS kernel formalizations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lord(K_t,Z_t,G,H_t) -> Proposal. It does not own the epistemic frame. ... S_t(K_t,Z_t,G,H_t,Proposal) -> Decision. Proposal != Decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives refined typed signatures for Lord (Lord(K_t,Z_t,G,H_t) -> Proposal, explicitly not owning the epistemic frame) and Sarathi (S_t(K_t,Z_t,G,H_t,Proposal) -> Decision), re-affirming Proposal != Decision as an important invariant, and situates both within a full epistemic control loop Observation -> Evidence -> Extraction -> Determination -> K_t -> {IdealState, Zero} -> Gap Delta_t -> Lord -> Proposal -> Sarathi -> Decision -> authorization -> Action -> new Observation -> K_{t+1}.

b_rows_sample.statement: Adds an explicit Policy parameter to Sarathi's signature, since choosing between 'investigate first' and 'accept uncertainty' depends on purpose, risk, authority, cost, governance and evidence policy that cannot be inferred from the Knowledge/Ideal/Zero/Lord state alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Instead of: Query -> Retrieve -> Answer
KnowledgeOS implements: Zero -> Gap -> Sarathi -> Retrieval -> Observation -> Evidence -> Knowledge -> Zero
This is a closed-loop epistemic investigation system, not a question-answering system.
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts RAG's open Query->Retrieve->Answer loop against a proposed closed-loop "epistemic retrieval loop" for KnowledgeOS: Zero detects a gap, Sarathi produces an investigation/retrieval plan, retrieval yields observations, observations become evidence, evidence updates the Knowledge State, and the updated state re-enters Zero -- framing KnowledgeOS as an investigation system rather than a question-answering system.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identifiable(g,Omega) quantifies over a world space W ... The canonical theory's eight-layer ontology ... has NO Omega. The property is therefore not FALSE in that theory; it is NOT STATABLE. ... therefore a layer is missing beneath Observation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 031 s31.17-31.21 gives a complete, correctly-quantified identifiability definition (Identifiable(g,Omega) iff for all W1,W2, Omega(W1)=Omega(W2) implies g(W1)=g(W2)) requiring the system to return Underdetermined when it fails; the audit could not see it because the canonical eight-layer ontology has no world-space W or observation function Omega, so the property is unstatable rather than false in that theory -- the correct conclusion is a missing ontological layer, not an inexpressible capability; Underdetermined (current-observation-relative) is distinguished from Non-identifiable (an information-theoretic limit that no further observation of the same kind can resolve).

type_signature.codomain: Bool, with a required Underdetermined return value

a_rows_sample.anchor: The three exclusions were a discovery failure, not a mathematical limit. They are absent from the AUTHORIZED MODEL v0.2 ... so the finding is real, and it is a GOVERNANCE finding: the constructions exist and were never promoted.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a prior verdict ('THEORY CLOSED AGAINST THE STATED CRITERIA -- NOT COMPLETE IN EVERY RESPECT', with 'a theory that cannot say nobody ever asked is closed, not finished') by showing the corpus does say 'nobody ever asked' (the not-assessed Zero-lens dimension state, committed one day before this programme began) and does have formal, typed constructions for non-identifiability and uncertainty; reclassifies the three exclusions as a discovery failure rather than a mathematical limit, and as a governance finding since these constructions are measured absent (zero grep occurrences of unknown/absent/not assessed/uncertain/identifiab) from the authorized v0.2 model despite existing in the raw corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The smallest missing thing is not a capability. It is a LAYER: the referent of knowledge. #1 (W,Omega) ... Nothing depends on it; everything below depends on it. ... Ordered, that is: (W,Omega) -> D_t -> AuthorityAct -> Sufficient -> delta-commit -> U-algebra. Two of the six require no invention at all -- they require adoption.
b_rows_sample.statement: Orders six missing concepts by dependency: (1) (W,Omega) the world and observation function -- nothing depends on it, everything below does; without it 'observation of what' is unanswerable, non-identifiability unstatable, Qualify has no semantics, and K's adequacy can only be scored not judged (CORPUS ESTABLISHES / NOT ADOPTED, nothing to invent); (2) D_t the recognised-dimension set (depends on #1) making 'not assessed' decidable (CORPUS ESTABLISHES / NOT ADOPTED); (3) AuthorityAct as an identity-bearing object (independent branch, equally blocking, NO CORPUS RESOLUTION, VERIFIER RECOMMENDS); (4) a typed Sufficient interface plus an evidence-independence relation (depends on #3 and on Evidence identity); (5) delta's commit case and a Gamma carrier in K (depends on #3); (6) U(H)'s algebra (depends on #1 for scope semantics); concludes two of the six (#1, #2) require only adoption, not invention.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'smallest-missing-concept-dependency-order' POSSIBLY relates to 'non-identifiability-omega-w' (batch B0041). Note: A dependency-ordered list of six missing concepts, concluding that (W,Omega) -- the world and the observation function, 'the referent of knowledge itself' -- is the single smallest missing concept, since everything else (non-identifiability, D_t's dimension semantics, Qualify's semantics, and K's adequacy being scorable-only-not-judgeable) depends on it; two of the six (W,Omega and D_t) require only adoption of already-existing corpus material, not invention.
