a_rows_sample.anchor: Can complex problem-solving vocabulary be decomposed into a small number of reusable semantic operations? That is a legitimate research hypothesis.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly connects to the earlier dhatu-extraction idea: whether complex problem-solving vocabulary reduces to a small number of reusable semantic 'atoms' (e.g. 'Just Start' -> INITIATE/ACT/REDUCE_DELAY/INCREMENT; 'Untangle Complexity' -> REMOVE/SEPARATE/SIMPLIFY/PRIORITIZE), explicitly not claimed as literal Sanskrit dhatus but as an analogous decomposition hypothesis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Does the text actually contain ten statistically distinct problem-solving mechanisms? ... Hypothesis A: distinct. Hypothesis B: several are manifestations of the same latent mechanism. Hypothesis C: some categories are actually orthogonal dimensions rather than categories.
a_rows_sample.statement: Three competing hypotheses about the author's ten-category taxonomy (distinct / collapsible / actually orthogonal dimensions like Action x Cognition x Constraint), with Hypothesis C called 'particularly interesting'; proposes testing rather than accepting the taxonomy via clustering on a constructed feature dataset (problem type, intervention, cognitive operation, action, constraint, feedback, outcome, iteration, uncertainty, data dependence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Problem solving becomes composition of semantic operators. ... Problem -> OBSERVE -> QUESTION -> REMOVE -> CONSTRAIN -> EXPERIMENT -> LEARN -> REFRAME -> ACT. A different problem might require: FILTER -> ACT -> OBSERVE -> LEARN -> AMPLIFY.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a small algebra of ten semantic operators (OBSERVE/QUESTION/FILTER/REMOVE/REFRAME/CONSTRAIN/ACT/EXPERIMENT/LEARN/AMPLIFY) from which any solution strategy is composed as a specific sequence, replacing a fixed ten-superpower methodology with operator composition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I1 -- Actionability ... I2 -- Feedback ... I4 -- Evidence skepticism: Data cannot automatically become truth. ... I7 -- Human agency: the book repeatedly treats creativity and problem-solving as human capabilities rather than purely mechanical optimization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven candidate Shani-style invariants for any problem-solving system extracted from the book: Actionability, Feedback, Reversibility/experimentation, Evidence skepticism (data != truth), Bounded complexity, Context-dependence, Human agency.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DATA != INTERPRETATION != ACTION != OUTCOME. ... data should pass through skepticism and other filters first. ... maps remarkably well to: OBSERVATION -> EVIDENCE -> INTERPRETATION -> DECISION -> ACTION -> OBSERVATION.
a_rows_sample.statement: The book's 'Question the Data' chapter reinforces Data!=Interpretation!=Action!=Outcome, mapped directly onto the KnowledgeOS Observation->Evidence->Interpretation->Decision->Action loop, suggesting the book could contribute a Problem-Solving Operating Model to KnowledgeOS with the existing constitutional architecture supplying governance constraints around it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not start by proving that Bashan is right. We should start with: What structure is actually present in the book? ... The Solution Mindset — Zero-Lens Structural Extraction v1.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the guiding methodological rule (extract structure first, test correspondence to the author's categories second, compress into an operator system third, generalize last) and proposes a concrete next artifact: a Zero-Lens structural extraction of all ten chapters without using the author's own category labels, to produce a clean dataset for the statistical/ML experiment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we must not discover a pattern and then validate it against the same evidence that created it. That is a major methodological principle for our project. ... training != model selection != test evaluation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the leakage/independent-evaluation invariant (already established for statistics generally in S0469/S0472) specifically for the semantic-operator discovery pipeline: SOURCE CORPUS->EXTRACTION->TRAINING DISCOVERY->LATENT OPERATORS->VALIDATION CORPUS->GENERALIZATION TEST.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 500 semantic operations ... compress them into 12 fundamental operators. We have performed a kind of semantic regularization. ... What is the smallest semantic operator set that retains predictive/explanatory power across independent problem-solving examples?
b_rows_sample.statement: 'Semantic regularization' concept: compressing many extracted semantic operations into a small operator set is formally analogous to model-complexity control, subject to the same bias-variance tradeoff (too few operators = oversimplification/high bias; too many = memorization/high variance), producing a formal research question about the smallest sufficient operator set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: discrete subset selection can have high variability whereas shrinkage is more stable. ... Hard semantic selection (KEEP/DISCARD) vs Soft semantic shrinkage (importance weighting). We should probably not immediately force a binary ontology.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes hard semantic selection (binary keep/discard of candidate operators) from soft semantic shrinkage (continuous importance weighting across frequency/strength/context-diversity/predictive-value/stability), recommending against forcing a premature binary ontology of semantic primitives.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The apparent 100-dimensional space could collapse to something like: Dimension 1 = Action/Inaction, Dimension 2 = Uncertainty/Certainty, Dimension 3 = Complexity/Simplicity, Dimension 4 = Evidence/Assumption, Dimension 5 = Feedback/Static reasoning. That would be far more profound than merely discovering ten categories.
b_rows_sample.statement: 'Semantic PCA' hypothesis: ~100 observable problem-solving features may reduce to a handful of latent bipolar dimensions (Action/Inaction, Uncertainty/Certainty, Complexity/Simplicity, Evidence/Assumption, Feedback/Static-reasoning), testable via covariance/principal-component analysis on vectorized problem-solving instances, with 80-90% explained variance by few dimensions as the success criterion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Model A semantic operator model, Model B topological model, Model C statistical feature model, Model D linguistic/dhatu model, Model E governance/invariant model ... epistemic ensemble learning. If five structurally different analyses independently identify FILTER/REDUCE/ACT/FEEDBACK/LEARN, then that convergence is considerably more interesting than a single clustering algorithm.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes 'epistemic ensemble learning': running five structurally independent analytical models (semantic-operator, topological, statistical-feature, linguistic/dhatu, governance/invariant) over the same material and treating cross-model convergence as stronger evidence than any single method's discovered structure, generalizing ensemble learning from prediction to epistemic corroboration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Linguistic reduction ... Structural reduction ... Statistical reduction ... test whether they converge: COMMON INVARIANTS. That is much more interesting than simply applying machine learning to a book. We are looking for cross-method invariants.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three reduction types (linguistic: sentence->verb->semantic-operation; structural: observations->latent dimensions; statistical: features->regularized model) and proposes their convergence as the target 'common invariants', reframing the whole research program as a search for cross-method invariants rather than single-method pattern discovery; closing recommendation to extract ESL's own operators (fit/select/regularize/shrink/partition/cluster/project/validate/bootstrap/ensemble/generalize) into the same representation used for Solution Mindset, producing a first cross-book operator matrix.

a_aliases: The Solution Mindset Zero-Lens Structural Extraction
b_aliases: Solution Mindset + ESL combined research stack

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'semantic-regularization-cross-book-research-architecture' POSSIBLY relates to 'problem-solving-semantic-operator-algebra' (batch B0012). Note: Combines 'The Solution Mindset' (qualitative problem-solving vocabulary) with 'The Elements of Statistical Learning' (quantitative discovery/validation machinery) into a three-layer research stack (qualitative operators + quantitative operators -> Zero Lens -> latent structure -> Shani/invariants); reframes the earlier semantic-operator-decomposition idea as 'semantic regularization' (compressing e.g. 500 semantic operations to ~12 fundamental operators, formalized as a bias-variance tradeoff: too few operators = high bias/oversimplification, too many = high variance/memorization) and a 'semantic PCA' hypothesis (many observable problem-solving features may collapse to a handful of latent dimensions such as Action/Inaction, Uncertainty/Certainty, Complexity/Simplicity, Evidence/Assumption, Feedback/Static-reasoning); proposes 'epistemic ensemble learning' -- running independent analytical models (semantic-operator, topological, statistical-feature, linguistic/dhatu, governance/invariant) and treating convergence across them as stronger evidence than any single method's output; refines the definition of Zero Lens from 'remove everything' to 'reduce a phenomenon to the smallest representation that preserves the distinctions necessary for explanation, prediction and validation' (minimal sufficient structure); distinguishes linguistic/structural/statistical reduction as three separate reduction types whose convergence identifies genuine cross-method invariants.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Proposition | A meaningful statement that can be true or false. | P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) ... Assertion | A proposition put forward as true, with a specific epistemic status... Knowledge | An assertion that satisfies the epistemic criteria for knowledge (justified true belief)
a_rows_sample.statement: Splits the Knowledge Atom into a three-level hierarchy Proposition subset-of Assertion subset-of Knowledge: Proposition=(E,D,V) is content without commitment; Assertion=(P,Sigma,Evidence,tau,Provenance) is a proposition put forward as true; Knowledge=(A,Justification,True) is a justified-true assertion; corrects the earlier Knowledge Atom to actually be an Assertion, not raw Knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Who determines True? KnowledgeOS observes, reconstructs, compares, challenges and guides. It generally cannot access Truth itself... Truth \neq Truth Assessment
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects making absolute Truth an internal primitive of Knowledge, since KnowledgeOS cannot access Truth directly; replaces the three-level model with four levels (Proposition -> Assertion -> Epistemically Accepted -> Reality/Omega), where 'Knowledge' becomes K=(A,Justification,TruthAssessment) rather than requiring literal correspondence to reality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation \rightarrow Candidate Proposition(s) ... because an observation can be ambiguous. ... 'Host responds on port 8081' -> P1/P2/P3
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects 'Observe -> Proposition' to 'Observation -> Candidate Proposition(s)', since one observation (e.g. a host responding on a port) can support multiple distinct, non-exclusive candidate propositions requiring Zero/Lord/Semantic-Reconstruction to disambiguate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = \mathcal{E}_t(\mathcal{A}_t) ... Knowledge isn't necessarily one object. It is a state of knowledge over many propositions and assertions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Knowledge from a single giant tuple to a Knowledge State K_t = E_t(A_t), an epistemic evaluation function over the set of currently available assertions A_t, foreshadowing K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,Observation_t,Zero_t,Lord_t,Evidence_t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: X_t \rightarrow O_t \rightarrow R_t \rightarrow A_t \rightarrow K_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the too-simple Reality->Observation->Knowledge pipeline into X_t (domain/reality) -> O_t (observation) -> R_t (semantic reconstruction/interpretation) -> A_t (assertion) -> K_t (knowledge state), with the critical point Observation ≠ Interpretation ≠ Assertion ≠ Knowledge, illustrated with the Bhīṣma example (seeing him = observation; 'Bhīṣma is a person' = interpretation; 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' = assertion; the same claim with provenance and epistemic qualification = knowledge).

a_rows_sample.anchor: P = \text{a semantically evaluable claim about entities, relationships, states or events}
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Proposition as a semantically evaluable claim (examples: IsOnBattlefield(Bhishma), GrandfatherOf(Bhishma,Arjuna), OpponentOf(Bhishma,Arjuna)), distinguished from Assertion: Proposition ≠ Assertion, and Assertion = Proposition + Epistemic Qualification + Provenance. Flagged as a distinction that 'should be frozen'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A_3 = Inference( A_1,A_2,\ldots, Rule, Assumptions, Provenance )
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends Infer(A_1,A_2,Rule)->A_3 to require every derived assertion to carry Rule, Assumptions, and Provenance so KnowledgeOS can explain 'why do you believe this?': every derived assertion traceable to source assertions + inference rule + assumptions + context, called essential for deterministic assurance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Document \neq Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the naive Documents->Chunk->Embedding->VectorDB->RAG->LLM architecture as 'not KnowledgeOS' because it bypasses the epistemic model: a document is not knowledge but an information-bearing source from which observations/assertions may be constructed — Document ≠ Knowledge, Document ≠ Evidence — illustrated by Document->Observation->Candidate Assertion->Evidence->Knowledge State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: LLM\ Output \neq Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Names three constitutional invariants for sources: (1) Source ≠ Knowledge (Document/API Response/Git Repository ≠ Knowledge); (2) LLM Output ≠ Knowledge — LLM Output -> Candidate Interpretation -> Epistemic Processing -> Knowledge; (3) Retrieval ≠ Knowledge Creation — Retrieve(Q) -> EvidenceCandidates -> Evaluate -> Knowledge. Overarching principle: 'Sources provide information; KnowledgeOS constructs governed knowledge from it. LLMs interpret; KnowledgeOS evaluates and governs. Retrieval supplies evidence candidates; it does not automatically create knowledge.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Interpret: Observation \times Context \rightarrow CandidateMeaning
a_rows_sample.statement: Interpret:Observation×Context->CandidateMeaning is where the structural parser, semantic parser, domain model, and LLM participate, worked through 'those with whom I have to fight' -> structural parsing -> semantic parsing -> candidate semantic structure -> candidate dimensions {Actor,Target,Action,Relationship,Obligation,Context} — explicitly 'not yet accepted knowledge'. CandidateAssertion=(Proposition,Sources,Interpretation,Context), e.g. 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' becomes a candidate proposition via Interpret->CandidateAssertions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assess: CandidateAssertion \times Evidence \times Rules \times Context \rightarrow EpistemicAssessment
a_rows_sample.statement: Assess:CandidateAssertion×Evidence×Rules×Context->EpistemicAssessment produces Σ_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) per explicit policy, contrasting e.g. (Acquisition=Reported,Support=Moderate,Uncertainty=Moderate,Validity=Current) against (Acquisition=AI-Generated,Support=None,Uncertainty=High,Validity=Unknown) depending on what actually supports the proposition. CandidateAssertion --Assessment--> Assertion=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID); K_{t+1}=δ(K_t,A). Full acquisition chain: X->Artifact->Observation->Interpretation->CandidateAssertion->Assessment->Assertion->K_{t+1}, stated to be 'already a computable architecture'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal P = \mathcal P_F \cup \mathcal P_N \cup \mathcal P_Q \cup \mathcal P_H \cup \mathcal P_I \ldots
a_rows_sample.statement: After ten tests, provisionally establishes 'Source Observation is computationally realizable' across documents, DB results, internet resources, human statements, LLM outputs, code, rules, ADRs, constitutions and instructions, preserving Source event ≠ Meaning ≠ Assertion. Surfaces two explicit unresolved theoretical points without deciding them: Open Point A — whether one Proposition abstraction P_F∪P_N∪P_Q∪P_H∪P_I∪... (factual/normative/definitional/instructional/question/hypothesis/interpretation) with an explicit semantic type suffices, versus needing genuinely distinct object types; Open Point B — whether the Observation model should stay unified (with acquisition method/type recording measurement vs statement vs database vs LLM etc.) rather than creating separate Observation concepts per source class.

a_rows_sample.anchor: one Proposition abstraction, with explicit semantic type.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses two explicit architectural-fork questions to the domain authority rather than deciding unilaterally: Question 1 — should factual/normative/definitional/instructional/hypothetical/interrogative content be different TYPES of semantic proposition under one common Proposition abstraction (recommended: Yes — one Proposition abstraction with explicit semantic type, rather than unrelated objects)? Question 2 — should the observation model stay unified, with acquisition method/type recording whether it came from measurement/database/document/human/LLM/API/parser (recommended: Yes)? If both are agreed, proposes formally closing Observation and moving to 'Computational Closure 2 — Interpretation', testing whether parsing+ontology+rules+LLM+human interpretation can transform arbitrary source observations into candidate semantic structures 'without pretending that interpretation is truth'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Should KnowledgeOS be allowed to create an Assertion with an explicitly unresolved epistemic state
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses and then answers the pivotal admission-boundary design choice: should an Assertion require passing a minimum admission threshold, or may it hold an explicitly unresolved epistemic state (Unknown/Hypothesized/WeaklySupported)? Recommends and then (in a 'Domain Authority' voice) DECIDES the latter: Assertion ≠ Proven Truth. Rationale given for rejecting the threshold alternative: it would remove Zero's ability to detect gaps (no representation for Unknown/Hypothesized), remove Lord's ability to generate candidates (no place for them to reside), sever the Observation->Interpretation->Candidate->Assertion provenance chain, damage auditability (no record of 'what we considered but did not accept'), make the incomplete-question problem unsolvable, collapse the Unknown-vs-Absent distinction, and break the learning trajectory Hypothesized->WeaklySupported->StronglySupported.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Truth = "This is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity."
a_rows_sample.statement: Re-runs all eight test cases (DB result -> StronglySupported; unstructured document -> WeaklySupported; internet page -> WeaklySupported with caveats; human statement -> Reported; LLM output -> Hypothesized; incomplete question -> no assertion created, Zero detects gap, clarification requested; conflicting sources -> both assertions remain in the Knowledge State with a detected Conflict; unknown value -> Assertion(Unknown)) through the new admission model. States the redefined meaning of 'the single source of truth': Truth = 'this is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity', NOT 'this is factually correct in reality' — the formalization of Knowledge ≠ Reality. Six constitutional invariants listed: Assertion≠Proven Truth; admission does not require verification; Unknown is a valid epistemic state (not absence of an assertion); epistemic status can evolve; multiple epistemic states can coexist (Conflicting is valid); provenance is preserved. Declares the Epistemic Admission Boundary computationally closed and proceeds to 'Computational Closure 3 — The Knowledge State'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A \not\equiv Truth(P)
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Assertion A=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID) with A≢Truth(P): A is 'KnowledgeOS's governed representation of P'. Two assertions of the identical proposition 'Nexus.version=3.69' can carry different epistemic states (Σ_A=(Observed,Strong,Low,Current) vs Σ_B=(Reported,Weak,High,Unknown)) and are 'not epistemically equivalent', giving Assertion⇏StrongEvidence, Assertion⇏Certainty, Assertion⇏Truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Admit(P,\Pi_1) \neq Admit(P,\Pi_2)
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces admission policy Π_adm with Admit(P_c,E,C,Π_adm)->{Assertion|Reject|Defer|RequestMoreEvidence}; admission is purpose-dependent, Admit(P,Π_1)≠Admit(P,Π_2) (an exploration policy may allow Weak support, a production-migration policy may require Strong support) — connecting directly to the Ideal State theory: an assertion can exist with Σ_K=Weak while the Ideal State requires Σ_I=Strong, producing a discrepancy rather than an invalid assertion. Distinguishes Admission ('may this proposition exist as governed knowledge?', Candidate->Assertion) from Validation ('does this assertion satisfy a particular requirement?', Assertion×Constraint->ValidationResult): Admission ≠ Validation — an assertion can be admitted (e.g. during discovery) yet later FAIL a validation (e.g. a migration requiring verified version) WITHOUT being deleted; it 'remains useful historical knowledge'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion \in KnowledgeState ... KnowledgeState \neq SetOfAssertions
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier equation Assertion=Knowledge (too strong) to Assertion∈KnowledgeState while KnowledgeState≠SetOfAssertions: the Knowledge State is a structured object K_t=(Assertions,Evidence,Relationships,Conflicts,Gaps,Provenance,Context,History,Constraints), 'a structured state, not simply a bag of claims' — called 'an important DDD correction'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Evidence is not a property of a document.}
a_rows_sample.statement: Central correction: Evidence is not a property of a document but 'a relationship between an observation and a proposition under a context and an evaluation rule' — Evidence(O,P,C,R). Prevents the mistake 'the document says X, therefore X is evidence [for whatever P]'. Gives Evidence≠Observation, Evidence≠Source, Evidence≠Support, Evidence≠Truth as four fundamental distinctions, and shows the SAME observation can be evidence for one proposition and not another (Evidence(O,P_1)≠Evidence(O,P_2)) — 'evidence is therefore relational'. E=(O,P,R,C,T,Q,Π): observation, target proposition, evaluation rule, context, temporal applicability, quality assessment, provenance.

type_signature.domain: observation x proposition x context x rule

a_rows_sample.anchor: Conclusion = Inference(Premises,Rule,Context)
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects 'the evidence voted for 3.69' informal aggregation, requiring Conclusion=Inference(Premises,Rule,Context) via an explicit inference rule (worked example: APIResponse.version=3.69 plus rule 'APIResponse(source=NexusProduction)=>CurrentVersion(NexusProduction)' yields the conclusion). Distinguishes four conclusion kinds: Deductive (Γ⊨P, entailed), Inductive (evidence increases support for a generalization without entailing it), Abductive (select the best explanation among hypotheses {H_1,...,H_n} — 'extremely relevant to KnowledgeOS'), Computational/derived (e.g. a version-vs-required-version comparison rule). Formalizes Conclusion object C_n=(P,Γ,R,κ,Σ,Π,t) (proposition, premises/evidence, inference rule, inference method, epistemic assessment, provenance, derivation time), letting KnowledgeOS answer 'why did you reach this conclusion?' not just 'what did you conclude?'.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'P=(E,D,V)'

a_rows_sample.anchor: We want to know whether there exists a corresponding state transformation T:K x I -> K such that F(That(H,i)) = T(F(H),i) for every valid H and input i. If this holds, then the history dynamics descend to the state space.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sets up the formal question of state sufficiency: given a history space H, a proposed state abstraction F:H->K, and a history-level transformation That:HxI->H, does a corresponding state-level transformation T:KxI->K exist such that F(That(H,i))=T(F(H),i) for all valid H,i -- i.e. do history dynamics descend to the state space.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H_A ~_F H_B iff F(H_A)=F(H_B). Then state sufficiency requires: H_A ~_F H_B => That(H_A,i) ~_F That(H_B,i). Thus ~_F must be a congruence with respect to valid transformations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the equivalence relation ~_F induced by the state abstraction (H_A~_F H_B iff F(H_A)=F(H_B)) and states the central congruence requirement: this equivalence must be preserved by every valid transformation for the state representation to be sufficient.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now suppose the proposed state representation retains only Content(K)={p}. ... Authorized(A)=true but Authorized(B)=false. Then F(That(H_A,validate)) != F(That(H_B,validate)). Yet initially F(H_A)=F(H_B). Content-only K fails the congruence test. This is a genuine falsification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsifies a content-only knowledge state via a worked example: two histories with different evidence sources (A authorized, B not) collapse to the same content-only state, but a governance-sensitive validation transformation produces divergent outcomes (Validated vs Unvalidated) depending on the discarded source information -- a genuine congruence failure, showing content-only K is insufficient once authority-sensitive transformations are valid operations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose we enrich the state with lambda(e)=source(e). Now F(H_A) != F(H_B) ... The previous counterexample disappears. But this does not yet prove sufficiency. We have only shown one missing distinction has been restored.
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows adding a source/provenance field lambda(e)=source(e) to the state resolves the specific counterexample found, but explicitly cautions this only restores one missing distinction and does not establish global sufficiency -- more collapsed-but-behaviorally-different histories must still be searched for.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose H_C and H_D have identical Content and Provenance. But H_C was produced under policy pi_1 while H_D was produced under pi_2 ... F(H_C)=F(H_D) under a representation that omits policy history. But T(H_C,i) != T(H_D,i). ... Is Policy part of state, provenance, or external context? ... It is de
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a further counterexample: two histories identical in content and provenance but produced under different policies collapse to the same state under a policy-omitting representation, yet future validation depending on the original governing policy produces different results -- concluding whether policy belongs to state, provenance, or external context cannot be decided by convenience but is determined by transformation sufficiency (independently arriving at a question the parallel verifier track, S1602/S1603, was also attacking).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two histories have the same proposition but different validity intervals theta_A(p)=[t0,t1), theta_B(p)=[t1,t2). Suppose a transformation asks CurrentVersion(S,t1+epsilon)? Then the two states produce different results. ... Temporal validity is not merely decorative metadata if temporal queries are
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows via a temporal-query counterexample (CurrentVersion(S,t1+epsilon)?) that a state representation omitting temporal qualification fails congruence when temporal queries are valid operations -- confirming temporal validity is functionally load-bearing, not decorative metadata.

a_rows_sample.anchor: e1->p and e2->not p. Compare K_A={p,e1} with K_B={p,e1,e2,not p}. A transformation T_assess may produce Assessment(K_A)=Supported but Assessment(K_B)=Conflicted. ... A state representation containing only the latest proposition K={p} would lose information necessary for future assessment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a contradictory-evidence counterexample showing evidence multiplicity is semantically relevant: two states differing only in whether conflicting evidence is retained produce different Assessment outcomes (Supported vs Conflicted) under T_assess, so a state keeping only the latest proposition would lose information needed for future assessment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose an information component x can affect the result of a valid future transformation T(K,i). Then x cannot be discarded from the state abstraction unless it is recoverable from other state information. Formally: x is semantically disposable => x=f(K) for some reconstruction function f, or no va
a_rows_sample.statement: States a general disposability criterion generalizing all the preceding counterexamples: an information component x may be discarded from the state abstraction only if it is reconstructible from the remaining state (x=f(K) for some f) or no valid operation can distinguish states differing only in x -- giving a formal test for classifying any candidate field as state, metadata, provenance, external context, or truly redundant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K=F(H) is a transformation-sufficient representation if all permitted future semantics can be determined from K, rather than the complete H. But we should not call K a sufficient statistic without qualification. ... K must be sufficient for the permitted KnowledgeOS transformation semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws an explicit but qualified analogy to the statistical notion of a sufficient statistic: a state K=F(H) is transformation-sufficient if all permitted KnowledgeOS transformation semantics can be determined from K rather than the full history H -- but the file cautions the statistical term applies to a specific model/parameter and should not be borrowed unqualified, since the KnowledgeOS requirement is broader (sufficiency for a whole permitted transformation semantics, not one parameter).

a_rows_sample.anchor: H ~ mu_H. Then K=F(H) induces a push-forward distribution mu_K = F_* mu_H. ... mu_K is a regime-level object, not necessarily part of K.
a_rows_sample.statement: Connects the state abstraction to measure theory without making it foundational: if H is a random history with distribution mu_H, then K=F(H) induces a push-forward distribution mu_K=F_*mu_H (mu_K(A)=mu_H(F^{-1}(A)) for measurable A); explicitly classifies mu_K as a regime-level object, consistent with the parallel Step 246 finding (S1601) that probability belongs to a regime projection, not to K itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F is a compression map. The question becomes: Is this compression lossless with respect to the semantics we care about? That is exactly the congruence question. ... F o That = T o F. This is the formal expression of state sufficiency.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the commutative-diagram criterion F o That = T o F as the formal expression of state sufficiency (the state abstraction F is a compression map; sufficiency means the compression is lossless with respect to the transformation semantics), calling it one of the strongest formal tests obtained in the corpus so far, and gives the corresponding failure interpretation (a non-commuting diagram means the proposed state representation has lost necessary information).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K=(Content,Qualification,Governance) survives the experiments only if those components contain all information required by valid transformations. ... we should not yet assert K=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) as a final decomposition. Instead: K must be defined by transformation sufficiency. This reverses
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the design question from 'what fields should a Knowledge State have?' to 'what information must a state preserve so that all valid KnowledgeOS transformations remain well-defined?'; explicitly withholds asserting K=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) as final until it survives transformation-sufficiency testing -- a route to the same skepticism about the 5-tuple that the parallel verifier track reached by counterexample.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Minimality = systematic removal + congruence testing. This is far stronger than selecting the smallest-looking tuple. ... Minimality is always relative to the transformation language. ... Minimality(K) = Minimality(K | T). There may be no context-free 'minimal Knowledge State.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates minimality testing as systematic per-component removal followed by re-checking the congruence criterion (F^{-i} o That = T^{-i} o F^{-i}), rather than choosing the smallest-looking tuple by inspection; states the important architectural corollary that minimality is always relative to the transformation language T (Minimality(K)=Minimality(K|T)) -- there may be no context-free minimal Knowledge State, since a richer future transformation set can make previously-discardable information necessary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Transformation-Sufficiency Proposition: T:K x I -> K is semantically well-defined with respect to That iff F(H1)=F(H2) => F(That(H1,i))=F(That(H2,i)) for all valid H1,H2,i. Equivalently F o That = T o F. ... not yet a proven KnowledgeOS theorem, because the full transformation set has not been estab
a_rows_sample.statement: States the phase's central named proposition (Transformation-Sufficiency Proposition), giving a single precise, computationally testable mathematical criterion for when a state-level transformation is semantically well-defined relative to a history-level one -- explicitly labeled not yet a proven theorem because the full KnowledgeOS transformation set has not itself been established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contr(p,K) iff Phi_conflict(p,P(p),K) = true. Where Phi_conflict evaluates positive under any of: Direct Negation Intersection (p and not-p asserted within identical context bounds); Inference Rule Clash (two derivation paths yield mutually exclusive conclusions via valid deduction); Source Provenance Incompatibility (mutually distrusted authority frames support opposing claims without a resolving meta-frame); Scalar Support Overlap (FDE Symptom): S+(p)>=tau_accept+ and S-(p)>=tau_refute-.
a_rows_sample.statement: Redefines Contr structurally: Contr(p,K) holds iff a conflict predicate Phi_conflict evaluates true over p, its provenance DAG P(p), and the knowledge state K, positive under any of four distinct conflict types -- Direct Negation Intersection, Inference Rule Clash, Source Provenance Incompatibility, or Scalar Support Overlap -- explicitly relabeling the last (the old S+/S- threshold test) as merely one observable FDE 'symptom' of conflict rather than the definition itself, correcting the earlier over-identification of Contr with scalar FDE arithmetic.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ASSERT ... risks confusing entity/proposition identity with assertion identity ... REVISE ... What exactly is being revised? proposition? assertion? evidence? interpretation? relation? evaluation? determination? These have different identities. A generic REVISE(p,...) is therefore probably too coarse ... RETRACT ... we still need to distinguish Retracted != Superseded != Invalidated != Expired != Withdrawn ... ISOLATE ... Still depends upon Scope(Contr(p),Gamma) and Contr and Scope are not fully determined. Therefore ISOLATE cannot be considered fully closed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies an unresolved identity question for four of the five O_core primitives: ASSERT risks conflating entity/proposition identity with assertion identity when a new independent assertion arrives about an already-existing proposition; REVISE is ambiguous about which of seven candidate objects (proposition, assertion, evidence, interpretation, relation, evaluation, determination) is actually being revised, making a single generic REVISE(p,...) too coarse; RETRACT needs to distinguish five different terminal states (Retracted, Superseded, Invalidated, Expired, Withdrawn) it currently conflates; ISOLATE cannot be closed while Contr and Scope remain undetermined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The 'monotonic delta' claim is mathematically misleading ... Nodes(K_t) subseteq Nodes(K_{t+1}) ... is not the same thing as monotonic knowledge. You have established at most: structural history monotonicity or append-preserving identity. It does not imply K_t <= K_{t+1} epistemically ... I recommend renaming Monotonic delta to History-Preserving delta or Append-Preserving State Transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a terminology overclaim: the node-set-inclusion property (Nodes(K_t) subseteq Nodes(K_{t+1})) is structural/append-preserving history monotonicity, not epistemic monotonicity (K_t <= K_{t+1} in a knowledge-ordering sense) -- a retraction, isolation, or revision can each reduce admissibility or invalidate a conclusion even while node-set inclusion holds. Recommends renaming 'Monotonic delta' to 'History-Preserving delta' or 'Append-Preserving State Transition' to state precisely what has actually been demonstrated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4.1 Aggregate Boundaries: KnowledgeCore (Aggregate Root) -- Nodes (Entities), Edges (Value Objects), Firewalls (Value Objects), Audit Log (Events). 4.2 Commands: type Command = ASSERT | LINK | REVISE | RETRACT | ISOLATE, each with typed fields. 4.3 Events: type DomainEvent = {type, nodeId, timestamp, stateHash, prevStateHash}. 4.4 Queries: type Query = QUERY | TRACE | EXPLAIN, explicitly separate from Command.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a concrete DDD implementation sketch not seen elsewhere in this batch: KnowledgeCore as an Aggregate Root containing Nodes (Entities), Edges (Value Objects), Firewalls (Value Objects), and an Audit Log (Events); a TypeScript discriminated-union Command type covering exactly the five O_core primitives with typed fields; a DomainEvent type carrying command type, node id, timestamp, and pre/post state hashes; and a Query type (QUERY/TRACE/EXPLAIN) explicitly kept separate from the Command/kernel layer, operationalizing the earlier decision to move read/observation operations out of the state-transition kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant 2.1.1 (Structural History Preservation): For all states K_t=<V_t,E_t,F_t,H_t> and operations o in O_core, the structural node set V and history ledger H are strictly monotonic: V(K_t) subseteq V(delta(K_t,o,Gamma)) and H(K_t) subseteq H(delta(K_t,o,Gamma)). Note: Epistemic standing S(p) is NOT monotonic under retraction or revision. Only physical history H and node presence V are monotonic.
b_rows_sample.statement: Implements the demanded 'Monotonic delta' correction precisely: splits the invariant into V(K_t) subseteq V(K_{t+1}) (structural node monotonicity) and H(K_t) subseteq H(K_{t+1}) (history-ledger monotonicity), explicitly stating epistemic standing S(p) is NOT monotonic under RETRACT or REVISE -- only physical history and node presence are monotonic, precisely the distinction the earlier reviews demanded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contract 1: ASSERT ... Preconditions: p not-in V(K_t) OR p in V(K_t) with status RETRACTED. Postconditions: p in V(K_{t+1}) ACTIVE ... Failure Semantics: If p in V(K_t) and status is ACTIVE, returns NO_OP_DUPLICATE. Contract 2: LINK ... Failure Semantics: raises UNMAPPED_NODE_EXCEPTION; transition aborts with K_{t+1}=K_t. Contract 3: REVISE ... Failure Semantics: If p is RETRACTED, raises REVISION_ON_RETRACTED_NODE_ERROR. Contract 4: RETRACT ... S(p) standing mass becomes <0,0,1.0> ... Failure Semantics: If p not-in V(K_t), returns NO_OP_NOT_FOUND. Contract 5: ISOLATE ... Failure Semantics: If scope is empty, defaults to local node isolation scope={p}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives each of the five O_core primitives a complete precondition/postcondition/failure-semantics contract with named failure outcomes not present in earlier versions: ASSERT returns NO_OP_DUPLICATE on a redundant active node; LINK raises UNMAPPED_NODE_EXCEPTION (aborting with no state change) if either endpoint is missing; REVISE raises REVISION_ON_RETRACTED_NODE_ERROR if the target is already retracted; RETRACT sets standing to fully-ambiguous <0,0,1.0> and returns NO_OP_NOT_FOUND if the target does not exist; ISOLATE defaults to single-node scope if no explicit scope is given.

It adds a member to the incompatible family rather than closing it: the recorded 19->17->6 contraction now has a 5 beside it, against 48 enumerations whose intersection is empty.
b_rows_sample.statement: Delivers this batch's single most consequential external correction: the C1-C4 assessment's self-declared O_core reduction to five primitives {ASSERT,LINK,REVISE,RETRACT,ISOLATE} matches NONE of the corpus's prior operator-count enumerations; rather than resolving the corpus's recorded operator-count contraction sequence (19 -> 17 -> 6), this batch's five-operator set is a 49th mutually incompatible enumeration added to a family of 48 whose collective intersection is empty -- meaning the batch's self-declared O_core closure did not converge the corpus's actual operator-registry debate, it extended its divergence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Transition \neq Overwrite ... K_{t+1} = Transition(K_t, Operation, Parameters) ... Observation, Semantic, Epistemic, Update, Comparison, Resolution, Navigation, History
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a state transition as a rule-governed operation transforming K_t into K_{t+1} (never overwriting), catalogs eight operation categories each with explicit preconditions/effects/postconditions (Observe, Detect, Parse, DiscoverDimension, DeriveProposition, Assert, Evaluate, ReEvaluate, AddEvidence, ChangeState, ReviseValue, Compare, DetectConflict, DetectGap, ResolveConflict, ResolveGap, Reframe, Prioritize, Query, Present, Preserve, Recall, Rollback).

a_rows_sample.anchor: There are actually three different concepts: Operation... Event... Transition. Operation -> Event -> StateTransition, not Operation=Transition. K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the model by separating Operation (a requested transformation command), Event (a record of what actually happened), and Transition (the function mapping state+event to new state): Command -> domain validation -> Event -> delta(K_t,e_t)=K_{t+1}, an event-sourcing/DDD pattern rather than treating operations as direct mutations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Compute != Change ... Decision != Commitment ... Only committed domain events change the Knowledge State ... Zero(K_t,I_t) -> Z_t, not K_{t+1} ... Zero should not automatically mutate K.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes Compute != Change and Decision != Commitment: analytical operations (Query, Compare, Evaluate, DetectConflict, DetectGap) must be pure computations returning results, never automatically mutating K_t; only an explicitly committed event changes the Knowledge State, reaffirming that Zero findings and Lord candidates are computed outputs, not knowledge mutations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H_t = {K_0,K_1,...,K_t} ... indexing problem... A cleaner formulation is H_{t+1}=H_t || e_t ... K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects History from a bag of full previous Knowledge-State snapshots {K_0,...,K_t} to an append-only event sequence H_t=(e_0,...,e_{t-1}), with the current state reconstructed via K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t) rather than stored redundantly -- providing auditability, reproducibility, and deterministic reconstruction as first-class properties.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rollback should NOT mean 'set current state back'... In an immutable history model you should not rewrite history... Rollback(K3,K1) creates a new transition K3->K4 where K4 approx K1 but K4 != K1 because they have different provenance/history. Rollback != TimeTravel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Rollback's semantics: since history is immutable and append-only, rolling back cannot delete or revert history; instead it produces a new state K4 structurally resembling an earlier state K1 but distinct from it by provenance -- Rollback != TimeTravel, Rollback = NewStateDerivedFromHistoricalState.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T1: Compute does not imply State Change. T2: Only committed events change K. T3: History is append-only. T4: Rollback creates a new state. T5: Zero evaluates Knowledge; Zero does not constitute Knowledge. T6: Lord proposes; Sarathi guides; the Knower/Agent commits. T7: K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t). T8: K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t).
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the entire state-transition correction into eight named theorems (T1-T8) as the bridge from the Questions 1-14 ontology to a KnowledgeOS epistemic state machine, changing the operating vocabulary from 'operations transform knowledge state' to 'committed epistemic events transform knowledge state; operations compute, propose, or request those events'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q18 should distinguish discovery from revision... Discovery -> Proposal -> Evaluation -> Authorization -> Revision ... Ideal State itself should have history: H^I_t, I_t=Replay(I_0,H^I_t,Pi_I). Ideal-State revision should itself be an event: I_{t+1}=delta_I(I_t,r_t).
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes symmetry between Knowledge-State and Ideal-State evolution: Ideal-State revisions must go through the same Discovery->Proposal->Evaluation->Authorization->Revision sequence as knowledge events, be recorded as an authorized IdealStateRevisionAuthorized event r_t, accumulate in an append-only Ideal-State history H^I_t, and be reconstructible via I_t=Replay(I_0,H^I_t,Pi_I) -- giving the Ideal State the same provenance/auditability the Knowledge State already has.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} = T(S_t, Operation, Policy, Evidence)
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the deepest missing mathematical point: the theory has many functions (Zero, Lord, Sārathi, DiscoverDimensions, Compare, Resolve, Present) but no algebra of state transitions. Proposes S_{t+1}=T(S_t, Operation, Policy, Evidence) with required properties: determinism where required, provenance preservation, invariant preservation, authorization, reversibility/compensation where applicable, versioning — 'where the theory becomes an actual formal system rather than a conceptual ontology'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 3 contains a feedback/cyclic system
a_rows_sample.statement: Verses 10-16's yajña cycle (Duty->Yajña->Rain->Food->Living Beings, tied back to prescribed action and Vedic direction) is read as a feedback/cyclic system, giving Action->Effect->SystemCondition->FutureAction, so ActionSystem=DynamicalSystem rather than a linear Workflow=Step1->Step2->Step3. Notes this supports event-sourced THINKING (S_n=fold(T,e_1,...,e_n)) but explicitly refuses the leap to 'therefore KnowledgeOS should use Event Sourcing' as an implementation conclusion the source does not support.

a_rows_sample.anchor: (K_t,Q,O,E,C) \rightarrow K_{t+1}
a_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts the bare LLM view y=f_theta(x) with a richer state transition (K_t,Q,O,E,C)->K_{t+1} (current Knowledge State, intent/question, observations, evidence, context), where the LLM is only one component producing the transition — 'LLM = one cognitive instrument used by the epistemic system', not 'LLM = intelligence'. Lists LLM roles as semantic parser, hypothesis generator, evidence interpreter, code generator, with KnowledgeOS deciding afterward whether output can become knowledge/an assertion, its provenance, supporting evidence, uncertainty, and conflicts — 'the missing governance layer'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Transition = (sourceState,targetState,rule,witness,time,actor)
b_rows_sample.statement: Emerging core primitive across all three cases: a Transition is the tuple (sourceState, targetState, rule, witness, time, actor).

b_rows_sample.anchor: It may be: Evidence-backed state transition. Knowledge is then one important semantic product of those transitions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Crucial architectural insight: the fundamental KnowledgeOS object may not be 'Knowledge' itself but the Evidence-backed state transition; Knowledge is then a semantic product of those transitions, not the primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Valid(\tau)= Precondition \land Rule \land Authority \land Witness \land TemporalValidity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Generic transition model: X_{t+1}=tau(X_t) only when Valid(tau)=1, where Valid(tau) = Precondition AND Rule AND Authority AND Witness AND TemporalValidity.

a_rows_sample.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Prior-family acknowledgement in Step 209: NONE. ZERO.
a_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-i): machine grep of Step 209 for the corpus's prior invariant-naming families (INV-n, AFR-0n, GT-0n, GG-/GE-/GC-/GA-, IR-0n, CM-0n, LA-0n, AAI, PLP, and bare C1-C7/S1-S6/K1-K7/V1-V10/I1-I20) finds zero matches of any kind; Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208, in its opening line) and nothing else. The prior families are independently confirmed present and locatable in the corpus (AFR-0* in 3 files, INV-1* in 1, GT-0* in 1, AAI in 2, PLP in 1, IR-0* in 1, CM-0* in 1, LA-0* in 1); none is reconciled, mapped, superseded, or mentioned. Also uncited: Step 048 (global invariants), Step 092 (invariant preservation), Step 025N (a prior 'algebra' -- Evidence Aggregation Algebra), Step 091 (safety/liveness ground for Step 209's own Sections 209.35-37).

a_rows_sample.anchor: IS IT AN ALGEBRA? NO.
a_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-ii): an algebra requires a carrier set, closed operations, and laws. Step 209 supplies none of the three properly: the carrier ('an invariant') is never typed and is used interchangeably as a predicate on states (I(s)), a proposition (I_1 ∧ I_2), and a named object (I_identity) within one file; the only operation is unqualified conjunction (I_global = AND of I_i), imported from propositional logic and never defined on the carrier; no laws are stated (no associativity, commutativity, identity element, closure, absorption, or distributivity). The only other algebraic-looking object, A = {C,I,S,T,R} (Section 209.34), is ill-typed: written in set-brace notation for what the surrounding text treats as an ordered heterogeneous 5-tuple, so it cannot support the componentwise access the text assumes. Verdict: Step 209 is a taxonomy plus a conjunction, mislabelled an algebra -- a useful, well-organised three-level taxonomy of invariants (local/context/system), not an algebra.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Satisfiability is declared and never tested
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.32 declares that I_global = AND(I_1..I_n) 'is only valid if the invariants are jointly satisfiable' and states SAT(I_1 ∧ I_2 ∧ ... ∧ I_n) 'is an important next mathematical direction' but never tests it: COMPUTABILITY verdict DEFINED, not CONSTRUCTIBLE (the I_i are natural-language predicates, not formulas in any decidable logic), not COMPUTED, not TESTED. Section 209.33 constructs a hypothetical unsatisfiable pair (Action->Approval vs Action->ImmediateExecution) and does not check it against the actual I_KOS set.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Cardinality drift: the 8-set I_KOS is silently superseded by a 15-list I1-I15 without amendment
a_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-iii): Step 209 Section 209.42 boxes and freezes an 8-member invariant set I_KOS = {I_identity, I_version, I_provenance, I_temporal, I_epistemic, I_authority, I_decision, I_execution}. Step 210 Section 210.25 then tabulates 15 invariants I1-I15 with no mapping given between the 8 and the 15. Independently checked: I13 (illegal transitions rejected) and I14 (preconditions/postconditions) have no member of I_KOS to belong to, and I15 (no semantic strengthening) is likewise unhoused unless forced into I_epistemic. The 8-set is silently superseded by the 15-list without amendment; only Step 209's own caveat ('we should not freeze this yet') prevents this from being an outright contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
a_rows_sample.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. Step 215 Section 215.24's ratios (182/43=4.233, 43/17=2.529, 17/8=2.125, 8/4=2.0, total 45.5x) make no arithmetic claim and are correctly disclaimed as unknown. Step 209 Section 209.42 vs Step 210 Section 210.25: |I_KOS|=8 vs |{I1..I15}|=15, difference 7, mapping absent (unreconciled).

a_rows_sample.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: I_L(A), I_C(BC), I_S(System); Execution cannot manufacture authority; Semantic Laundering; I_KOS 8-set
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 ('Invariant Algebra') stratifies invariants into local/context/system levels (I_L, I_C, I_S); defines Verified(E)⇒Provenance(E)∧Integrity(E), Valid(A)⇒EvidenceBasis(A)∧ModelVersion(A), Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D), Executed(X)⇒Authorized(X) boxed as 'Execution cannot manufacture authority'; an epistemic partial order and knowledge lattice; 'Semantic Laundering' (a downstream context losing provenance/uncertainty of an upstream claim and treating the result as stronger than warranted); 'Determinism != Correctness'; architecture-as-CSP A={C,I,S,T,R}; safety properties P1-P4 and liveness properties L1-L2; and the boxed 8-member frozen set I_KOS={I_identity,I_version,I_provenance,I_temporal,I_epistemic,I_authority,I_decision,I_execution}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY: 1 (Step 208 only); LATER RESPONSE: Step 210 replaces I_KOS with I1-I15 without amendment
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208) and zero prior invariant families. Later response in scope: Step 210 Section 210.25 replaces the 8-member I_KOS with a 15-row I1-I15 without amendment; Step 210 Section 210.9 restates Step 209's Section 209.25 semantic-strength principle as Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION VERDICT: REFRAMES; DEFINITION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_CLEAR with one ILL-TYPED object
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 reframes scattered '!=' observations into a stratified system but does not resolve the SAT question it raises nor reconcile with any prior invariant family. CLEAR: the three-level stratification, Executed(X)⇒Authorized(X), semantic laundering, determinism!=correctness. ILL-TYPED: A={C,I,S,T,R} uses set-brace notation for an ordered heterogeneous 5-tuple, which has no positional structure though the surrounding text requires componentwise access. NOT_DEFINED: the type of 'an invariant' itself, used as a predicate on states, a proposition, and a named object within one file. INCOMPLETE: I_KOS's eight members are one-word labels with no formulas, unlike the file's own worked examples.

a_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 209.32 (conjunction written as established, satisfiability tested after, never run)
a_rows_sample.statement: I_global = AND_{i=1}^n I_i (Section 209.32) is written as an established equality, and the satisfiability precondition (SAT test) is stated only afterward, as future work, never run. If the I_i are not jointly satisfiable then I_global is identically false and the boxed I_global = AND(I_KOS) is an assertion of contradiction. Everything downstream that treats I_global as a satisfiable target -- Step 210's matrix, Step 211's AAG, Step 212's gap register -- is conditional on repairing this. Secondary: Section 209.14's determinism claim (SameState+SameCommand⇒SameDomainResult) is used inconsistently as assumption, requirement, and derived property without saying which.

a_rows_sample.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: nothing reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE; TEST VERDICT: NOT_EXECUTED
a_rows_sample.statement: I_L/I_C/I_S stratification is DEFINED; I_KOS's 8 members are DEFINED but not INPUTS_KNOWN (unformalized); SAT(I_1∧...∧I_n) and SAT(A) are DEFINED but not CONSTRUCTIBLE (natural-language predicates, no decidable-logic encoding, and A is ill-typed); P1-P4/L1-L2 are DEFINED, self-described as 'candidates, not yet final requirements'; delta(A_t,c), Pre, Post are DEFINED with no aggregate instantiated. The file's own Section 209.34 concedes 'this is not yet a complete formal verification system.' Test verdict NOT_EXECUTED -- P1-P4 are called 'excellent candidates for deterministic assurance tests', none written or run.

a_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG; MEASUREMENT VERDICT: MIXED with a good refusal and a violation
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209's separation of probabilistic inference from deterministic governance (Section 209.15), Determinism!=Correctness (Section 209.16), InvalidModelApplication!=LowConfidence (Section 209.17, a genuinely important distinction between model misspecification and wide posteriors), HighUncertainty!=KnownIncorrect / LowUncertainty!=GuaranteedTrue (Section 209.18), and ObservedCorrelation⇏Causation (Section 209.29, uncited against Step 074) are all statistically correct. Measurement: Section 209.21 correctly declines to universalize a total order on epistemic strength (Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported, 'should not be interpreted as a universal total ordering') -- a good refusal -- but Section 209.25 then writes S(T(x))>S(x), a strict comparison requiring exactly the order just declined, four pages later with no reconciliation. KnowledgeState=(EvidenceStrength,Consistency,Uncertainty) is correctly presented as a partial order/lattice admitting incomparable elements, with no arithmetic attempted (correct). I_global=AND(I_KOS) conjoins a nominal set of one-word labels that are not propositions -- a type gap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG on structure, WEAK on consistency boundaries; UL: 'Semantic Laundering' the best-defined new term
a_rows_sample.statement: The I_L/I_C/I_S stratification is textbook-correct and the clearest statement of the aggregate/context/system-invariant distinction in the corpus; Section 209.6 correctly identifies Decision.AssessmentRef⇒Resolvable(AssessmentRef) as crossing aggregates, but DDD's standard remedy (a consistency-boundary decision -- strong vs eventual consistency, process manager/saga) is never offered, despite the corpus already containing '# Step 166 — Process Managers, Sagas' (uncited). 'Semantic Laundering' (Section 209.24: 'a downstream context loses the provenance or uncertainty of an upstream claim and treats the transformed result as stronger than its source warrants') is judged the single best-defined new term in the band; against this, I_KOS's eight members enter the language as labels without definitions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS: conjunction cannot express the dependency graph the file itself draws
a_rows_sample.statement: Stated assumptions: invariants are propositions closed under AND; a single global conjunction is the right composition; governance transitions can be made deterministic. Hidden: that conjunction is the only composition operator needed, despite Section 209.31's dependency graph showing invariants depending on one another (a relation AND cannot express) -- Sections 209.31 and 209.32 are structurally inconsistent, a dependency graph is not a flat conjunction (Internal Contradiction #B); that the I_i are mutually independent, contradicted by 209.31; that I_KOS's eight members cover the space, with no completeness argument (Step 210 immediately produces 15). Undefined symbols: Integrity(E), EvidenceBasis(A), AssessmentMethod(A), DecisionBasis(D), ApplicablePolicy(D), Resolvable(.), Traceable(D,Basis(D)), Basis(D), S(x), EvidenceStrength/Consistency components, Eventually(.), and every member of I_KOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 209
a_rows_sample.statement: Survives: the three-level invariant stratification; Semantic Laundering; Determinism!=Correctness; InvalidModelApplication!=LowConfidence; Execution cannot manufacture authority; identity continuity independent of state continuity; the safety/liveness lens; the insight that a constitution should constrain invariants, not technologies. Does not survive: the title (it is not an algebra); A={C,I,S,T,R} as typed; SAT(A) as computable; I_global=AND(I_KOS) as a verified-satisfiable object (unverified, and structurally at odds with the dependency graph of Section 209.31); S(T(x))>S(x) as a well-formed comparison.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The symbol I is silently rebound between Step 208 (information measure) and Step 209 onward (invariant) with no announcement
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Evidence/Test ordering is reversed between files, and Step 210's own boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own tuple
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209's tail agenda for 210 orders Invariant->Owner->EnforcementPoint->Test->Evidence->FailureMode; Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple orders enforcement, monitoring, test, failure (test before the implied evidence); but Step 210's own boxed Section 210.40 conclusion states Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance (evidence before test); Step 211 Section 211.2 (boxed) and Step 214 Section 214.2 (boxed) both revert to Test before Evidence. Four sources agree that Test precedes Evidence; Step 210's one boxed conclusion disagrees with all of them, including with its own tuple -- the direction matters (Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test; Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout). This is Contradiction #5.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A and Gap: eight bindings of A, four bindings of Gap with two different ordinal category sets
a_rows_sample.statement: A denotes: Assessment (208-212, throughout), an aggregate state A_t (209.13), the architecture-as-CSP set A (209.34), an assurance vector (211.9), an AI-artifact 7-tuple (211.21), a statistical-result 8-tuple (210.13), an architecture snapshot A_t (213.16-18), and an artifact A_j (213.4) -- eight bindings, with Section 209.13's aggregate-state A_t formally indistinguishable in notation from Section 213.17-18's architecture-state A_t (delta(A_t,c)=A_{t+1} vs A_0->A_1->...). Gap denotes: a numeric difference (211.4, 212.10), an ordinal category (211.4's {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} vs 212.10's different {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown}), a class (212.11 G1-G5), and a register row (212.31 G-01-G-15) -- four bindings, with the two ordinal category sets differing from each other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #15 — Total order on epistemic strength declined in Step 209 Section 209.21 and then used in 209.25 and 210.9
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.21 states Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported and explicitly declines a universal total ordering ('the actual epistemic lattice must be derived from the domain'). Step 209 Section 209.25 (S(T(x))>S(x)) and Step 210 Section 210.9 (Strength(T(x))>Strength(x)) both then use strict > on the same kind of quantity, presupposing the order that was just declined four sections earlier and never derived. Severity MEDIUM.

b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.1 boxes V_i = (I_i, O_i, E_i, M_i, T_i, F_i) (invariant, owner, enforcement mechanism, monitoring mechanism, test/verification, failure behaviour) but the rendered matrix has only 4 columns (ID, Invariant, Owner, Verification) realizing I_i, O_i, T_i -- E_i (enforcement), M_i (monitoring), and F_i (failure behaviour) are absent for all 15 invariants: 45 of the declared tuple components are unrealized. b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210's Verification column lists 15 test names verbatim (identity transition test, version reconstruction, lineage traversal, semantic contract test, negative inference test, payload/semantic test, reproducibility test, privilege-path test, failure simulation, outcome verification, conflict test, historical replay, state-machine test, invariant test, transformation test) with zero results, zero of the fifteen tests existing as code, and none run (confirmed by Part 2's zero-executable-fences finding). b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD CATEGORY ERROR IN THE 'Owner' COLUMN
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 206 Section 206.15 derives the candidate bounded-context set as Observation, Evidence, Assessment, Governance, Decision, Execution. Step 210's Owner column instead contains values like 'Domain' (a layer), 'Persistence/Domain' (two layers), 'Knowledge infrastructure' (a layer), 'Assessment/Contracts' (half artifact-kind), 'Aggregate' (a tactical pattern, not a party), and 'Contracts' (an artifact kind). b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 ('Invariant Verification Matrix') defines a 6-tuple V_i=(I_i,O_i,E_i,M_i,T_i,F_i) per invariant; boxes 'Architectural Principle != Architectural Property' and 'No claim of architectural compliance without identifiable evidence'; defines Reachable(D,E)!=empty; boxes 'Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity' and 'Epistemic state cannot be silently strengthened'; states Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); boxes 'Quantitative value without relevant uncertainty may constitute semantic loss'; defines a statistical-result 8-tuple A=(theta-hat,Estimator,Sample,Population,Model,Assumptions,Uncertainty,Validity); boxes 'Documentation < ExecutableEvidence < FormalProof'; a conceptual Assurance(I)=f(Evidence,Coverage,Independence,Repeatability,Criticality); an E_1..E_5 evidence hierarchy (documentation..formal verification); the target for-all-s-in-S_reachable: I(s)=True; and boxes 'AI may assist assurance; AI should not be the sole source of assurance', plus the 15-row invariant-verification matrix itself (60/60 cells filled).

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION/DEFINITION VERDICT: CLEAR on the principle/property distinction, CONTRADICTORY on E_1..E_5 (twice)
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 answers 'where' (role names) and 'how proven' (test names) but not 'is it true' for any invariant. CLEAR: the principle/property distinction (its best contribution), Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity, the three assurance levels. INCOMPLETE: V_i is 6-ary, only 3 components ever instantiated. AMBIGUOUS: 'Owner' is used as bounded context, layer, pattern, and team interchangeably. CONTRADICTORY: E_1..E_5 vs Step 212's E_0..E_5 (Contradiction #3), and E_1 bound to two incompatible types within Step 210 itself (Contradiction #4: Section 210.20's evidence-item E_1 vs Section 210.30's documentation-rung E_1).

b_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 210.30 vs 210.20 (E_n ambiguity); honest gaps in 210.26/210.28/210.29
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 210.20 uses E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P as evidence items; Section 210.30, ten sections later, binds E_1=documentation...E_5=formal verification as evidence-strength levels -- the same subscripted symbol carries two incompatible types with no disambiguation, and every downstream use of E_n in Steps 212-214 inherits the ambiguity. Section 210.29 honestly declines to scalarize Assurance and names fake precision (Assurance=97.3%) as a hazard, yet Section 210.28 immediately prior writes Critical(I)⇒HigherAssurance(I), a comparison requiring the very ordering Section 210.29 declines. Section 210.26 correctly concedes a test provides evidence, not proof (Test(I_8)=PASS does not prove I_8=True in all states), then Section 210.32's target for-all s in S_reachable: I(s)=True leaves S_reachable undetermined (Section 210.33 concedes this openly) -- an honest, correctly-labelled gap, not an invalidity.
